title: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core
summary: LLM agents that act on live Web data must combine heterogeneous evidence, remember what they have done and improve from outcomes without weakening their own safeguards. We study this problem in autonomous investing, where every action is irreversible and based on untrusted Web content. We present Steward, a multi-agent LLM system that draws the boundary of self-evolution in its type system. First, nine role-specialised agents decide jointly: four analysts read news feeds, SEC filings, macroeconomic series and market data and emit typed reports, from which a Portfolio Manager sets target positions that a protected Risk Manager audits. Second, a seven-layer shared memory, assembled by code from the system's own record, gives each decision its position context, the market narrative, calibration and the agent's past decisions. Third, the system improves itself by review: code grades every trade and forecast nightly and writes the grades into memory, and each quarter a reflector proposes prompt learnings that a deterministic gate applies reversibly and replay of recorded inputs verifies. All three operate around an invariant core of order arithmetic, risk rules and discipline-agent prompts that no self-edit can reach. In a five-month live deployment (102 trading days, 1,632 LLM calls), the system contained a 24.6% sector drawdown to a 0.3% loss; in replay of its recorded inputs, a single model given the same raw data traded more and lost 1.35 points against the market over five days where the joint design showed no significant loss, and no injected instruction was followed; and a 2015-2026 backtest shows the core alone lowering the maximum drawdown under all 50 random entry policies. The reflector traced the dominant failure to its root cause, and the gate applied a learning that the agent adopted on trigger evenings and on no control evening. Code: https://github.com/yebof/quant-agent
core_methodology: Steward is a multi-agent LLM system designed for autonomous investing, featuring role-specialized agents (analysts, portfolio manager, risk manager) that process heterogeneous data sources, a seven-layer shared memory for contextual decision-making, and a self-improvement mechanism through nightly trade reviews and quarterly reflector proposals. The system operates around an invariant core of order arithmetic and risk rules that cannot be altered by self-editing.
data_sources: News feeds, SEC filings, macroeconomic series, market data, and the system's own recorded inputs for replay and verification.
alpha_potential: The system demonstrates robust performance in live deployment and backtesting, effectively containing drawdowns and improving decision-making through self-review and adaptive learning. Its multi-agent approach and invariant core provide a disciplined framework for generating alpha while managing risk.
title_cn: 治理式自主投资的自我进化：具有不变核心的多智能体LLM系统
summary_cn: 本研究提出Steward系统，一种基于多智能体LLM的自主投资框架，通过角色专业化分工（分析师、组合经理、风控）处理多源数据，结合七层共享记忆实现上下文决策，并通过夜间交易评审和季度反射器提案实现自我进化。五个月实盘测试显示其成功控制回撤，核心规则不可修改的设计保障了系统的稳健性。

title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting
summary: Most contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems are released with frozen parameters and improve through external updates, whereas an ideal system would keep improving from its own experience, a capacity we call recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet studying RSI requires an environment that is continuously changing, objectively verifiable, and naturally grounded, posing a fundamental challenge for agent evolution. Here we introduce EvoForesight, a sustainable evolution agent system grounded in future event prediction, in which agents continuously interact with a dynamically evolving environment and improve by internalizing and externalizing the experience gained through these interactions. A living environment synthesizes verifiable tasks, and a recursive-evolution engine turns the reasoning trajectory behind each prediction back into capability: decoupling search from prediction adapts parameter-level evolution to the contamination-prone live environment, while distilling reusable skills lets the agent evolve from the limited live trajectories such an environment affords. On the external FutureX leaderboard, which evaluates predictions against real-world outcomes and is updated weekly, our self-improved forecaster ranked first across all systems over three consecutive weeks, achieving up to a 195% improvement in rating. On our synthesized evaluation, it ranked among the top three across four base LLMs, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 10.7 Bradley--Terry points. More broadly, these results suggest that a system built for self-improvement is best understood as an agent that co-evolves with a genuinely living, open-ended environment, pointing to a shift in AI from training static models on fixed data toward cultivating agents that grow stronger from their own experience, with such an open world as the indispensable basis of that growth.
core_methodology: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) through continuous interaction with a dynamically evolving environment, combining future event prediction with agent evolution. The system decouples search from prediction and distills reusable skills from limited live trajectories.
data_sources: Real-world outcomes for validation (FutureX leaderboard) and synthesized evaluation tasks, updated weekly to reflect new data.
alpha_potential: High potential for predictive modeling in financial markets by continually adapting to new data and improving forecasting accuracy. The system's ability to internalize and externalize experience could create adaptive trading strategies that outperform static models.
title_cn: 与开放世界共同进化：面向未来预测的递归自我改进
summary_cn: EvoForesight系统通过递归自我改进（RSI）技术，在动态变化的环境中持续优化预测能力。其核心是将搜索与预测解耦，并从有限的实际轨迹中提炼可重用技能。在金融交易领域，该系统可开发出自适应市场变化的量化策略，通过持续学习新数据提高预测准确性，相比传统静态模型具有显著优势。测试中该系统在真实环境预测任务中实现了195%的性能提升，展现出强大的金融时间序列预测潜力。

title: Intraday Forecasting Ability and Liquidity Provision of Institutional Traders
summary: This study uses a high-frequency dataset from a stock exchange to examine how forecasting ability and liquidity provision relate to institutional traders' proprietary intraday profitability. We discover persistent forecasting abilities among traders. Specifically, we demonstrate that hypothetical flow-following strategies based on the execution flows of these skillful traders yield annualized Sharpe ratios ranging from 16 to 63 across various trading frequencies. We match buy and sell executions into positions, linking realized profit and loss (P&L) to horizon-matched forecasting proxies and the liquidity roles of both executions. Our findings indicate a direct correlation between improved forecasting ability and profitability, where a one-standard-deviation increase in the forecasting ability proxy is associated with 1.02 -- 1.19 currency units higher P&L per matched position. Additionally, we measure liquidity-provision intensity within a matched position by its number of passive executions: zero, one, or two. In these regressions, P&L is 1.28 -- 1.31 currency units higher for one passive execution than for none, and a further 3.79 -- 3.82 higher for two than for one, underscoring the significant financial benefits of liquidity provision.
core_methodology: The study analyzes high-frequency trading data to link institutional traders' forecasting ability and liquidity provision to their profitability. It employs flow-following strategies based on execution flows of skilled traders and measures liquidity-provision intensity by counting passive executions within matched positions.
data_sources: High-frequency dataset from a stock exchange, including execution flows and P&L data of institutional traders.
alpha_potential: The paper identifies a direct correlation between forecasting ability and profitability, with significant financial benefits from liquidity provision. The annualized Sharpe ratios of 16 to 63 suggest strong alpha potential, especially in high-frequency trading environments.
title_cn: 机构交易者的日内预测能力与流动性提供
summary_cn: 本研究通过高频数据揭示了机构交易者的预测能力与流动性提供对盈利的直接影响。采用基于熟练交易者执行流的跟随策略，年化夏普比率达16至63。流动性提供的强度与盈利显著正相关，具有实际交易应用价值。

title: Uncertainty and Explainability in Deep Rough Volatility: A Neural Information-Theoretic Posterior Approach
summary: Deep learning has substantially accelerated the calibration of complex stochastic-volatility models, but neural point calibration alone does not capture the uncertainty remaining after an implied-volatility (IV) surface has been observed. We develop a simulation-based inference framework for rough Heston (rHeston) calibration that learns the posterior distribution of the model parameters conditional on an IV surface. Using neural ratio estimation, we obtain calibrated posterior samples that can be propagated through heteroscedastic neural surrogate pricers for path-dependent exotic options. The resulting posterior-predictive distributions combine residual parameter uncertainty with conditional surrogate uncertainty and yield uncertainty-aware price intervals. We further introduce Hellinger-SHAP, an information-theoretic explainability method for posterior inference. Rather than attributing a single parameter point estimate, it applies local-background Kernel SHAP to a posterior-information functional measuring contraction from the prior to the posterior. This identifies maturity--moneyness regions associated with posterior information gain for individual rHeston parameters. In a simulation study, posterior-predictive intervals provide calibrated or conservative coverage across forward-start, barrier, and realized-variance claims, while point plug-in prices can be materially unreliable for selected contract regimes. Together, the UQ and XAI analyses provide a transparent framework for uncertainty-aware neural calibration and downstream exotic pricing under the specified prior-predictive model.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a simulation-based inference framework for rough Heston model calibration using neural ratio estimation, which learns the posterior distribution of parameters conditional on an implied volatility surface. It also develops Hellinger-SHAP, an information-theoretic explainability method for posterior inference.
data_sources: Implied volatility surfaces from options markets, used to calibrate the rough Heston model parameters.
alpha_potential: The methodology provides uncertainty-aware price intervals for exotic options, combining parameter uncertainty with surrogate model uncertainty. This can improve pricing accuracy and risk management for path-dependent derivatives, potentially identifying mispriced contracts.
title_cn: 深度学习粗糙波动率中的不确定性与可解释性：一种神经信息理论后验方法
summary_cn: 该论文开发了一种基于模拟的推断框架，用于粗糙Heston模型的校准，通过神经比率估计学习参数的后验分布。结合Hellinger-SHAP可解释性方法，为路径依赖型奇异期权提供不确定性感知的价格区间，提高了复杂波动率模型在衍生品定价中的实用性和透明度。

title: DiffLTM: Continuous Diffusions Large Tabular Models for Conditional Generation
summary: Conditional generation is a key capability to be supported by Large Tabular Models, enabling a number of applications. Accurate conditional generation has to contend with two key challenges: $(i)$ Data comprise a mixture of numerical and categorical entries, the latter often with high cardinality and heavily unbalanced proportions; $(ii)$ Conditional generation becomes increasingly difficult for rare sub-populations. The best models in this class use a hybrid of continuous and discrete diffusions. In this paper, we design a continuous diffusion model with strong generation quality. An important element is the use of cross-entropy loss for categoricals, for which we provide a first theoretical justification. We introduce metrics that focus on rare subpopulations. Further, we generalize conditional generation techniques to enable new types of conditioning. Finally, we show that our model (trained on labor data) can capture classical insights from econometrics. Code is available at https://github.com/granica-ai/DiffLTM
core_methodology: Continuous diffusion model for conditional generation of mixed numerical and categorical data, with theoretical justification for cross-entropy loss in categoricals and novel metrics for rare sub-populations. Enables new types of conditioning and shows ability to capture econometric insights.
data_sources: Labor data (as shown in the paper), but methodology is generalizable to mixed financial datasets containing both numerical (e.g. prices/returns) and categorical data (e.g. sector/industry classifications).
alpha_potential: Could generate synthetic market scenarios for stress testing, create augmented datasets for training ML models on rare market conditions (e.g. crashes, squeezes), or conditionally generate alternative data patterns for strategy development. Particularly valuable for modeling tail events and rare market regimes.
title_cn: DiffLTM：基于连续扩散的大表格模型条件生成方法
summary_cn: 扩散模型处理混合数据类型，实现高质量条件生成，特别关注小概率事件。可应用于极端市场情景的合成数据生成与策略测试，经济计量学验证体现金融应用潜力。

title: Future of Time Series Anomaly Detection: From Historical Review to Unified Outlook
summary: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) is a foundational problem in data mining, aiming to identify observations that deviate significantly from nominal temporal patterns. Driven by escalating data volumes and application complexity, recent research has yielded diverse architectures, including diffusion models, state space models, and large language models (LLMs). However, existing surveys provide limited coverage of these emerging designs and lack a unified treatment of multivariate anomalies, cross-domain unified modeling, metric reliability, and contemporary evaluation challenges. To bridge these gaps, this survey delivers three core contributions: (1) We establish a refined anomaly categorization and a structured taxonomy of paradigms reflecting modern advances, comparing detection mechanisms and charting developmental trajectories across paradigms. (2) We provide an extensive analysis of evaluation methodologies and conduct comprehensive experiments to assess metric fidelity, complemented by an open-source benchmark repository encompassing algorithms, datasets, and evaluation tools. (3) We outline key open challenges, offering forward-looking perspectives on dynamic thresholding, model interpretability, zero-shot transfer, multi-modal alignment, and foundational models for time series. By addressing existing theoretical and empirical limitations, this survey establishes a coherent framework to guide future TSAD research and practical deployments.
core_methodology: The paper presents a comprehensive survey of time series anomaly detection (TSAD) techniques, including modern architectures like diffusion models, state space models, and large language models (LLMs). It provides a structured taxonomy of paradigms and evaluates various detection mechanisms and evaluation methodologies.
data_sources: The survey likely covers a wide range of time series data sources, including but not limited to financial time series (e.g., stock prices, trading volumes). The specific datasets are part of their open-source benchmark repository.
alpha_potential: TSAD techniques can be valuable for identifying anomalous market behaviors, unusual trading patterns, or structural breaks in financial time series, which can be leveraged for alpha generation through event-driven strategies or adaptive models.
title_cn: 时间序列异常检测的未来：从历史回顾到统一展望
summary_cn: 本文综述了时间序列异常检测的最新方法，包括扩散模型、状态空间模型和大语言模型等新兴架构。对金融时间序列分析（如市场异常检测、交易模式识别）有显著应用价值，可为量化交易策略提供理论基础和实践指导。

title: Solvable models of learning to pursue a moving target
summary: Agents tasked with intercepting a moving target must learn how to reach it, ideally as efficiently as possible. As observers of animal pursuit behavior have noticed, different strategies are possible: on one extreme, the agent reactively moves toward the target's current location; on the other, the agent predicts the target's future location and moves directly there. Motivated by the desire to understand how such strategies might be learned, we introduce a continuous-time linear-quadratic model of open-loop target pursuit whose optimal control strategies interpolate between these possibilities. Usefully, a small number of interpretable parameters control which type of strategy is optimal, and it is possible to derive closed-form solutions for optimal strategies, policy learning dynamics, and value learning dynamics. Exploiting our model's linear structure, we find that the time scales of learning precisely correspond to the eigenvalues of certain matrices, and that relevant eigenvalue spectra generically have a gap. We show that this gap indicates that agents tend to learn how to reach their target before optimizing their movement. Our results provide a detailed mathematical characterization of pursuit behavior and its learning dynamics, which can both serve as a benchmark for empirical work, and as a foundation for more elaborate theoretical treatments of pursuit.
core_methodology: Continuous-time linear-quadratic model of open-loop target pursuit with closed-form solutions for optimal strategies and learning dynamics
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any time series data of moving targets (could be applied to price movements, order flow, or other financial time series)
alpha_potential: Potential application to momentum trading strategies by learning optimal pursuit strategies for price movements, with particular relevance to algorithmic execution and predictive trading strategies
title_cn: 可解的学习追求移动目标模型
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种连续时间线性二次模型，用于学习最优追踪策略，在金融领域可应用于价格动量追踪、算法执行和预测交易策略。模型能够产生闭合形式的解决方案，并揭示学习动态，有助于设计自适应市场追踪算法。

title: Doubly Robust Distributionally Robust Offline Contextual Pricing
summary: Offline contextual pricing often relies on logged observational data, but faces challenges from distributional shifts between training and deployment environments. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provides a principled approach to off-policy evaluation and learning (OPE/L). However, existing methods are mostly limited to discrete actions. Recent work has explored DRO for continuous treatments using inverse propensity weighting (IPW), while such IPW-based estimators can be sensitive to the convergence rate of propensity score estimates, particularly when estimated nonparametrically, which may lead to larger estimation errors and regret. In this work, we develop a doubly robust (DR) framework for distributionally robust OPE/L in continuous pricing settings. For evaluation, we propose a localized DR estimator that addresses the computational challenges of worst-case expectations by fitting only a small number of regressions, comparable to standard non-robust DR, while achieving semiparametric efficiency under mild product rate conditions. For learning, we leverage the inherent smoothness of demand noise to handle pricing-specific discontinuities in revenue outcomes (e.g., threshold-based purchase decisions), establishing a finite-sample regret bound of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_p(T^{-s/(2s+1)})$ for smoothness orders $s=1,2$. This bound improves upon existing regret rates in existing DRO-based off-policy learning (OPL) for continuous treatments. Extensive experiments under various levels of distribution shift validate our proposed framework.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a doubly robust (DR) framework for distributionally robust off-policy evaluation and learning (OPE/L) in continuous pricing settings. It addresses computational challenges in worst-case expectations by using localized DR estimators and leverages the inherent smoothness of demand noise to handle pricing-specific discontinuities in revenue outcomes.
data_sources: Logged observational data from pricing experiments or historical pricing data, likely including contextual features and purchase decisions.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to optimize pricing strategies in financial markets, such as setting bid-ask spreads or algorithmic trading execution prices, by accounting for distributional shifts and improving robustness to market regime changes.
title_cn: 双重稳健的分布鲁棒离线上下文定价
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种双重稳健框架，用于处理连续定价中的分布偏移问题。通过局部化双重稳健估计器，解决了最坏情况期望的计算难题，并在需求噪音的平滑性基础上处理定价收益的不连续性。该方法可应用于金融市场中的定价优化，如算法交易执行价格的设定，提高对市场环境变化的鲁棒性。实验验证了在不同分布偏移水平下的有效性。

title: DISC: Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost for Time-Series Dataset
summary: The growth of time-series datasets and foundation models has made dataset comparison a central part of time-series workflows. Assessing source-target transfer before model adaptation requires similarity estimates that can summarize transfer-related dataset relationships without exhaustive source-target evaluation over every candidate pair. Many metrics have been proposed for measuring similarity between time-series datasets, but they capture different dataset relationships and vary in how well they align with downstream utility across tasks. We evaluate this gap by measuring the correlation between source-target similarity scores and downstream forecasting errors in out-of-distribution and transfer-learning settings. We propose Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost (DISC), a learnable aggregation framework that uses calibration transfer observations to select, weight, and combine similarity metrics for different downstream tasks. By integrating complementary metric values, DISC better distinguishes source-target dataset differences that matter for downstream behavior. After calibration, DISC scores source-target pairs using only their similarity-metric values and yields higher alignment than single-metric references on the reported split. These results show that time-series dataset similarity is task-dependent, and that learned metric integration provides a stronger proxy for downstream transfer behavior than manually selecting one similarity metric.
core_methodology: The paper proposes DISC (Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost), a learnable framework that combines multiple similarity metrics for time-series datasets to better predict downstream task performance in transfer learning settings. It optimizes the selection and weighting of similarity metrics to align with forecasting accuracy.
data_sources: Not explicitly specified, but methodology is applicable to any time-series datasets including financial time-series (e.g., price, volume, economic indicators).
alpha_potential: The methodology could improve performance in two key areas: 1) Selecting most relevant historical periods/markets for time-series forecasting models, and 2) Evaluating and selecting data sources for transfer learning applications in finance (e.g., adapting models across assets or market regimes).
title_cn: 时间序列数据集分析的领域集成相似性成本方法
summary_cn: 该研究提出的DISC框架可优化金融时序数据的迁移学习方案，通过智能加权组合多种相似性指标，能更准确地预测不同市场周期或资产间的模型迁移效果，有望提升多因子模型的稳定性与跨市场套利策略的收益风险比。

title: S$^2$-MAS: A Society-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation Framework with 500 Million Household Persona Agents
summary: Simulating economic responses at society scale requires agents whose decisions reflect household circumstances and the effects of earlier actions. We introduce S$^2$-MAS, a society-scale multi-agent simulation framework built on 500 million synthetic household personas grounded in real-survey data. Its Genese engine separates decisions from state updates, while reusable financial scenarios and application ledgers track consumption, cash, debt and payments. Trained with SFT + RLCD on 2.93 million examples, sharp-421m-mlx achieves 74.55% accuracy and 38.37% question-macro F1 on one-shot consumer financial-choice tasks derived from held-out survey responses. Its accuracy exceeds GLM-5.3-Flash, Jev 1.13, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GPT-6-Luna and GPT-6-Astra in the common benchmark (full test for the first four; matched 500-group sample for Astra). We evaluate eight financial task families and simulate 12 million distinct household agents in paired purchase-funding conditions. Jointly raising purchase goals and approved credit limits increases consumption, with responses differing across age and income groups. Education, employment and household-size differences persist after age-income standardization and mainly reflect transitions from deferral to purchase. Asset and debt groups differ in cash drawdown, repayment and closing debt. A response-stratified 24-month panel varies purchase goals under a common credit product, with repayment and arrears updating subsequent offers. S$^2$-MAS links heterogeneous household decisions to evolving consumption, cash and repayment paths, supporting economic experiments across household groups, population scales and time horizons.
core_methodology: Society-scale multi-agent simulation with 500 million synthetic household personas, trained using SFT + RLCD on real-survey data, with a Genese engine that separates decisions from state updates and tracks financial metrics.
data_sources: Real-survey data for household personas, including financial scenarios and application ledgers tracking consumption, cash, debt, and payments.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to simulate heterogeneous household decisions and financial behaviors at scale can uncover macro-level trends and micro-level anomalies in consumer behavior, which could inform trading strategies in consumer credit markets, retail sector investments, and macroeconomic forecasting.
title_cn: S$^2$-MAS：基于5亿家庭角色代理的社会规模多Agent模拟框架
summary_cn: 该研究通过大规模多Agent模拟（500万家庭角色）分析消费者金融行为差异，可应用于零售信贷策略优化、消费周期预测及宏观经济因子挖掘。其金融场景复用和分层决策机制为量化交易提供了微观行为数据支持的仿真环境。

title: Eluder-Dimension-Free Regret for Stage-Wise Constrained Contextual Bandits via Offline Regression
summary: Contextual bandits with stage-wise constraints model decisions that must control risk while learning from their outcomes. We study this problem when only the selected action's reward and cost are observed, with a general reward class and a convex class of nonlinear cost functions. We propose CS-UCCB, which combines offline regression, cost confidence sets, and upper counterfactual confidence bounds. Each regression fit defines a valid cost confidence set, while a geometry derived from covering entropy controls cumulative cost uncertainty along the sampled decisions. Under polylogarithmic covering entropy for both classes and polylogarithmic offline estimation error, the finite-action algorithm guarantees, with high probability, feasibility at every round and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sqrt T)$ regret without an eluder-dimension term. We also extend the analysis to infinite actions under an explicit reward-design condition and compare our bound with existing eluder-dimension bounds.
core_methodology: CS-UCCB combines offline regression, cost confidence sets, and upper counterfactual confidence bounds to solve contextual bandit problems with stage-wise constraints. The method uses polylogarithmic covering entropy and offline estimation error to ensure feasibility and optimal regret bounds.
data_sources: Theoretically, this can be applied to any financial data where actions (e.g., trades) have associated rewards (e.g., returns) and costs (e.g., transaction costs or risk metrics).
alpha_potential: The method's ability to handle constrained optimization with nonlinear costs could be valuable for developing trading strategies that need to balance returns against various risk metrics or transaction costs, particularly in high-frequency or algorithmic trading contexts.
title_cn: 通过离线回归实现无Eluder维度的阶段约束上下文赌博机遗憾
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种结合离线回归和成本置信集的方法CS-UCCB，用于解决具有阶段约束的上下文赌博机问题。在金融交易中，该方法可用于开发需要在每步交易中控制风险并优化回报的策略，尤其适用于高频交易和算法交易中的风险回报平衡。

title: Directionally Correct Views in Portfolio Optimization
summary: Portfolio optimization techniques often use historical data to estimate parameters for Markowitz-type or ML models. Effective allocation requires a way to align the available data with conditions expected over the investment horizon. Inspired by the Black-Litterman framework, we ask whether incorporating expert views leads to better portfolio allocations. In a simple Markowitz setting, we show that even a small amount of directionally correct information can materially improve investment decisions. We also discuss how expert views can be incorporated in end-to-end portfolio models using entropy-based ideas. Somewhat surprisingly, our empirical results indicate that simpler Markowitz-type model perform as well as an end-to-end model, once directionally correct experts are incorporated.
core_methodology: The paper uses a Markowitz-type portfolio optimization framework enhanced with directionally correct expert views, similar to the Black-Litterman approach. It also explores entropy-based methods for incorporating expert views in end-to-end portfolio models.
data_sources: Historical market data and expert views (qualitative or directional inputs from financial experts).
alpha_potential: Improves portfolio allocation by combining quantitative models with qualitative expert insights, potentially capturing market inefficiencies not fully reflected in historical data alone.
title_cn: 投资组合优化中的方向正确观点
summary_cn: 该研究探讨在Markowitz模型中加入方向正确的专家观点是否能提升投资决策。结果表明即使少量专家的方向性建议也能显著改善组合配置。方法结合定量模型与定性输入，对开发融合人类洞见的量化策略具有实用价值。

title: SpecMAGIC: Specification-Guided Multi-Task Generalization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Multi-task generalization is an important yet underexplored problem in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). Many real-world applications require multi-agent systems to generalize across complex, temporally extended tasks with diverse inter-agent coordination requirements. We introduce a specification language that combines temporal-logic task specifications with operators for expressing such requirements. We propose SpecMAGIC, a hierarchical framework that leverages the automaton structure of task specifications for subtask decomposition. A centralized high-level planner identifies and allocates compatible subtask sequences across agents, while decentralized low-level policies execute individual subtasks. This enables zero-shot generalization to new tasks by composing reusable subtask policies according to new specifications, without retraining. We establish soundness and probabilistic completeness of the high-level planner. Experiments on multi-agent navigation tasks show that SpecMAGIC substantially outperforms existing approaches on unseen task specifications and maintains strong performance as the number of agents increases.
core_methodology: Hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with centralized planning and decentralized execution, leveraging temporal-logic specifications for task decomposition and zero-shot generalization
data_sources: Multi-agent navigation tasks (simulated environment)
alpha_potential: Potential application in multi-agent trading systems for portfolio rebalancing or execution strategies where agents need to coordinate across complex, temporal tasks without retraining
title_cn: SpecMAGIC：基于规范的多智能体强化学习中的多任务泛化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一个基于规范语言的分层框架，通过中央规划与分散执行实现多智能体系统在复杂时态任务中的零样本泛化。在量化交易中可应用于需要多策略协同的智能交易系统架构设计，特别是对组合再平衡、订单执行等需要时态协调的场景具有潜在应用价值。

title: FIGFLEX: A Mixed-Precision FP-INT GEMM Accelerator Co-Designed with Low-Bit LLM Quantization
summary: Weight-only quantization keeps LLM activations in floating point and stores weights as low-bit integers, turning the dominant workload into floating-point-integer (FP-INT) general matrix multiplication. Recent quantizers reach a 2-3-bit average with mixed precision, but hardware has not kept pace: GPUs dequantize weights to FP16 before the tensor-core multiply-accumulate, and bit-parallel FP-INT accelerators run at a single weight precision, so fewer bits save memory but not computation. In this paper, we present FIGFLEX, an algorithm-hardware co-designed mixed-precision accelerator whose bit-parallel datapath scales throughput as precision falls. FIGFLEX contributes (1) a shift-add, radix-4 reformulation of FP-INT multiplication that fuses the multiply-accumulate into a unified, precision-flexible partial-product reduction and roughly halves the partial products, together with a novel INT3 optimization that reclaims the idle datapath radix-4 leaves at that precision; and (2) a mixed-precision quantizer that assigns each channel group its bit-width according to the error GPTQ cannot compensate, with a per-input-channel column scaling whose power-of-two normalization keeps the scaled activations out of the FP16 subnormal range, so that the quantized model maps directly onto FIGFLEX's datapath with the same accuracy as on a GPU. On LLaMA-2-7B, FIGFLEX attains 5.85 and 8.77 WikiText-2 perplexity at 3- and 2-bit average precision, lower than GPTQ, AWQ, SliM-LLM, AMQ, and QuIP# (without fine-tuning), while delivering 1.56x and 1.42x higher whole-chip throughput per area on the linear GEMMs of a 3-bit mixed-precision model than AxCore and FIGLUT, respectively.
core_methodology: Presents a mixed-precision FP-INT GEMM accelerator co-designed with low-bit LLM quantization, using a shift-add, radix-4 reformulation of FP-INT multiplication and a mixed-precision quantizer for efficient computation.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to work with large language models (LLMs) like LLaMA-2-7B, which can be adapted for financial text/data processing.
alpha_potential: Potential for faster and more efficient processing of large-scale financial data using quantized LLMs, which can be leveraged for sentiment analysis, news-based trading strategies, or other NLP applications in finance.
title_cn: FIGFLEX：一种与低比特LLM量化协同设计的混合精度FP-INT通用矩阵乘法加速器
summary_cn: FIGFLEX通过混合精度FP-INT通用矩阵乘法加速器和低比特量化技术的协同设计，提高了大型语言模型的计算效率。这种技术在金融领域的应用潜力在于加速金融文本数据处理，可能提升基于NLP的交易策略执行速度，如新闻情绪分析或财报数据处理。

title: When News Gets Old: Portfolio Allocation with Reinforcement Learning and Large Language Models
summary: Financial news can influence investment decisions long after publication. Timely news may reach an investor before prices fully adjust, whereas older news may already be reflected in prices. We examine two ways to handle aging signals: retain them and give a portfolio policy timing information, or filter them out before portfolio selection. A fixed large language model (LLM) extracts signals from public SEC disclosures. We compare these treatments in reinforcement learning (RL) policies and LLMs that choose portfolios directly. We evaluate returns after trading costs in historical tests over 2023-2025. RL choices respond to timing information in a controlled test, but historical returns show no consistent benefit from adding it. For the LLM, filtering old news produced the highest average net return, reaching 18.43% per year when news delivery was delayed by four weeks. This exceeded the returns of all RL strategies that used news.
core_methodology: Combines large language models (LLMs) for news sentiment analysis with reinforcement learning (RL) for portfolio allocation, specifically examining how to handle aging news signals by either retaining them with timing information or filtering them out.
data_sources: Public SEC disclosures (financial news/regulatory filings), historical market data (2023-2025 period)
alpha_potential: Seeks alpha through delayed market reaction to news (4-week delay showed best results). Potential signal comes from market underreaction to SEC disclosures filtered by LLMs.
title_cn: 当新闻变旧时：基于强化学习与大语言模型的投资组合配置
summary_cn: 本研究通过大型语言模型(LLM)提取SEC披露文件的信号，结合强化学习处理新闻时效性问题。实证表明，过滤陈旧新闻策略(延迟4周处理)年化收益达18.43%，优于其他处理方式。为新闻驱动的量化策略提供实践框架。

title: TT-SAX: A Two-Track Time Series Symbolization for Natural Language Shape Querying
summary: Natural language querying for time series databases aims to let users find what they need in long histories of data by asking in plain language. Shape queries ask how a series moves. They are the main challenge of this task. Recent work makes them feasible by using symbolization as a bridge between the query and the long history. However, existing symbolizations were designed for compression, similarity indexing, or classification. What a symbolization should provide for natural language querying has not been systematically studied. We therefore examine the definitions of six classical symbolizations against this task and identify three limitations. (1) Direction is missing from the string, (2) direction is measured at too small a scale, and (3) the letters are arbitrary. Three design principles follow. We follow these principles and make a minimal redesign of SAX called TT-SAX (two-track SAX). The level letters stay. Each segment gains a trend letter. It is measured across neighboring segments rather than inside one, and graded to match the adjectives that queries use. We conduct extensive experiments on the public NLQTSBench benchmark, comparing TT-SAX with the six classical symbolizations across six LLMs. TT-SAX outperforms all six on shape queries, and ablations trace its gains back to the three limitations one by one. This paper is the first systematic study of time series symbolization with natural language querying as the design goal. It provides a foundation for future research on this task. Our code is available at https://github.com/Atlamtiz/tt-sax.
core_methodology: TT-SAX is a novel time series symbolization method that extends SAX (Symbolic Aggregate Approximation) by incorporating trend information across neighboring segments, making it more suitable for natural language shape queries. The methodology focuses on capturing directional trends at an appropriate scale and using graded trend letters to match natural language descriptors.
data_sources: The paper evaluates TT-SAX on the public NLQTSBench benchmark, which includes various time series datasets. While not finance-specific, the methodology is applicable to financial time series data such as stock prices or economic indicators.
alpha_potential: TT-SAX's improved shape querying capability could potentially be used to develop more intuitive and effective querying systems for financial time series, enabling traders to quickly identify patterns or trends in historical data using natural language. This could enhance pattern-based trading strategies or assist in exploratory data analysis for financial research.
title_cn: TT-SAX：用于自然语言形态查询的双轨时间序列符号化方法
summary_cn: TT-SAX通过改进SAX方法，在符号化过程中加入跨段的趋势信息，更适用于自然语言的形态查询。该方法可应用于金融时间序列数据，帮助交易员以自然语言快速检索历史数据中的特定价格形态，或用于开发基于形态识别的交易策略。

title: Interpreting Model Reasoning through Behavioral Counterfactuals
summary: Faithfully understanding the internal process that occurs as models form their chain of thought is an important problem with the rise in model capabilities. However, this remains challenging due to the variance in sampled responses, making it difficult to isolate the effects of interventions and compare model reasoning systematically. We propose a method for localizing and analyzing how a given intervention affects the model's reasoning through behavioral counterfactuals: given a fixed response, how does introducing an intervention to the prompt change the next-token distributions? We train a module to edit the residual stream such that it minimizes the KL divergence between the output distributions for a fixed response under a source prompt and its counterfactual target prompt. We find that matching the output distributions recovers the counterfactual behavior more effectively than standard activation reconstruction objectives and validate that attribution of the trained module outputs is effective for identifying causally important locations for counterfactual recovery. The attribution maps and visualizations of the downstream effects of model edits provide an interface for generating hypotheses about the original model's computation, which can then be tested with activation patching. In a case study on Gemma-4-E4B-it and DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B, we investigate how a suggestion influences model reasoning even when it is not verbally acknowledged. Our analysis identifies representations at the question statement and filler tokens that mediate a substantial part of the suggestion's influence, with downstream effects such as changing the framing of the justification or even the final answer.
core_methodology: Behavioral counterfactuals for analyzing and editing model reasoning by minimizing KL divergence between output distributions under source and counterfactual prompts
data_sources: Experimental analysis on Gemma and DeepSeek models, not specific financial data
alpha_potential: Potential for improving interpretability and control of financial LLMs in trading signal generation, though requires adaptation to financial contexts
title_cn: 通过行为反事实解释模型推理
summary_cn: 该研究提出了基于行为反事实的模型推理分析方法，通过编辑残差流匹配输出分布，可有效追踪模型决策路径。在量化交易中，此技术可用于解析金融大模型的信号生成机制，增强交易策略的可解释性和可控性，但需针对市场数据专门适配。

title: Fast Iterative Combinatorial Auctions via Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Iterative combinatorial auctions are used in spectrum allocation, transportation, and industrial procurement, but rounds are costly. We introduce FastCombo, a deep reinforcement learning approach to sequential price discovery. Bayesian pricing has sharply reduced auction rounds even against subgradient benchmarks tuned with hindsight for each instance, but relies on a one-step objective and repeated online inference and optimization. We prove that greedily maximizing immediate clearing probability can require arbitrarily more rounds in expectation than an informative policy, even with the true valuation distribution known. FastCombo learns price policies offline, assigning credit to queries for the future decisions they enable and producing each online price update with a single neural-network forward pass. We formulate the objective of minimizing expected rounds to clearing in single-minded auctions as a partially observable Markov decision process and train a recurrent bidder-item graph policy over complete auction trajectories. In a one-item experiment, all five trained policies learn an informative opening, reducing expected rounds from 1.85 to 1.65 relative to the tested Bayesian one-step rule. Across four domains from the Combinatorial Auction Test Suite, FastCombo achieves competitive clearing while reducing measured online price-selection time per auction by a factor of roughly 300-900 relative to the standard Bayesian baseline. These results demonstrate the value of learning sequential price policies for both information acquisition and online computational efficiency.
core_methodology: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approach for sequential price discovery in iterative combinatorial auctions, formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) with a recurrent bidder-item graph policy.
data_sources: Not explicitly financial market data, but based on experiments using the Combinatorial Auction Test Suite, simulating auction environments relevant to spectrum allocation, transportation, and industrial procurement.
alpha_potential: Potential application in designing sophisticated auction mechanisms for financial instruments or dark pool trading, particularly where multi-round price discovery is essential. The approach could be adapted for dynamic pricing of illiquid assets or package deals in financial markets.
title_cn: 基于深度强化学习的快速迭代组合拍卖
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种深度强化学习方法FastCombo，用于多轮组合拍卖中的序列定价优化。通过将拍卖过程建模为部分可观察马尔可夫决策过程，并训练循环神经网络策略，显著提高了定价效率。虽然直接应用于金融交易需要调整，但该方法在暗池交易、大宗交易等需要复杂价格发现的金融市场场景中具有潜在应用价值。

title: An Introduction to World Models for Generalist Agents
summary: World models have recently emerged as a promising direction toward developing generalist agents capable of understanding, predicting, and interacting with diverse environments. However, despite growing interest, the concept of a world model remains loosely defined, encompassing approaches ranging from predictive dynamics models and learned simulators to models that jointly generate future observations and actions. This introductory paper aims to clarify the concept of world models and provide a unified perspective on their role in developing generalist agents. Starting from the partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) framework, we connect world modeling to classical control, dynamical systems, signal processing, and reinforcement learning. We introduce different approaches to world modeling, emphasizing the knowledge they capture, their learning objectives, and how they support decision-making. We further explore the relationship between world modeling and policy learning, highlighting how these capabilities can be unified through conditional prediction without requiring separate models. Rather than offering an exhaustive survey of existing methods, this paper focuses on fundamental concepts, modeling principles, and connections, with the goal of providing an accessible and unified introduction to world models for generalist agents.
core_methodology: The paper discusses world models, which are frameworks for creating generalist agents capable of understanding and predicting diverse environments. These models are based on partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) and integrate concepts from classical control, dynamical systems, signal processing, and reinforcement learning. The methodology emphasizes conditional prediction for decision-making without requiring separate models.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology implies the potential use of any sequential or time-series data, which could include financial market data for trading applications.
alpha_potential: World models could potentially be applied to financial markets to create adaptive trading agents that can predict market dynamics and optimize trading strategies in real-time, exploiting temporal patterns and market inefficiencies.
title_cn: 通用智能体的世界模型导论
summary_cn: 本文探讨了世界模型作为开发通用智能体的框架，其能理解和预测多样化环境。应用于金融交易，这些模型可能通过强化学习和时间序列预测优化交易策略，实时适应市场动态。

title: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
summary: Scientific discovery often requires identifying a small number of high-performing designs in vast, constrained search spaces. This is difficult when evaluations are costly, feasible solutions are sparse, parameters are strongly coupled, and physical constraints are strict. Recent AI for AI methods can automatically improve algorithms and optimization procedures. However, general purpose approaches are not designed around scientific priors, physical constraints, and limited evaluation budgets. We introduce ADAPT for Science, a multi-agent framework that treats scientific optimization as two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search. ADAPT uses historical designs to identify promising and diverse initial conditions, progressively concentrates computation on favorable search directions, and evolves the optimization procedure from execution feedback. We evaluate ADAPT on the design of gravitational wave detectors using a differentiable physics simulator and eight unseen detector topologies. Under matched scientific evaluation budgets, ADAPT achieves a mean loss of 0.204 +/- 0.101, reducing loss by 54.9% relative to the best classical optimizer and by 62.2% relative to the best general purpose agentic evolution baseline. ADAPT achieves the lowest loss on all unseen topologies among the evaluated baselines. ADAPT provides a step toward scientific optimization systems that continuously learn from prior experience and their own search outcomes.
core_methodology: Multi-agent framework for scientific optimization that combines historical design analysis with adaptive search direction concentration and optimization procedure evolution based on execution feedback
data_sources: Physics simulator data (gravitational wave detectors in paper), but methodology could theoretically be applied to financial market data
alpha_potential: Potential for portfolio optimization or parameter search in trading systems where evaluations are expensive (e.g., backtesting complex strategies), and for identifying sparse high-performing configurations in large search spaces
title_cn: ADAPT科学应用：用于自进化科学优化的多代理系统
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种多代理框架，通过结合历史设计分析和自适应搜索方向优化，在受限搜索空间中高效寻找最优解。尽管针对科学优化设计，其方法论可应用于量化金融领域，如在高成本回测条件下优化交易策略参数或投资组合配置。系统能在评估预算有限时快速收敛的特性对算法交易尤其有价值。

title: MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback
summary: Mix-policy optimization incorporates off-policy expert data into the reinforcement learning (RL) loop to transcend the capability boundary of on-policy RL. However, existing methods either provide static full-trace guidance that suppresses self-exploration, or adopt expert prefix guidance without correctness guarantees, leading to suboptimal performance or even training collapse. In this paper, we propose MOER, a mix-policy optimization framework that harmonizes expert guidance with self-exploration. MOER injects a decaying expert chain-of-thought prefix into the prompt and lets the model complete the remaining reasoning, with the prefix length progressively annealed to encourage self-exploration. A selective rollback mechanism replaces failed completions with the original full expert trace, guaranteeing the correctness of every off-policy trajectory. Furthermore, a harmonized mix-policy objective optimizes on-policy tokens with a GRPO loss while supervising both expert prefix and completion tokens with a trust-region SFT loss, substantially stabilizing training. Extensive experiments show that MOER achieves the highest average scores in mathematical and general domain reasoning tasks, outperforming all basic and mix-policy baselines, and generalizes consistently across diverse tasks, model scales, and base model categories. Codes are available at https://github.com/CityU-MLO/MOER.
core_methodology: MOER is a mix-policy optimization framework that combines expert-guided reinforcement learning with self-exploration. It uses a decaying expert chain-of-thought prefix in prompts, progressively encouraging self-exploration while ensuring correctness through a selective rollback mechanism. The framework employs a harmonized mix-policy objective with GRPO loss for on-policy tokens and trust-region SFT loss for expert-guided tokens.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but the methodology is generic and could be applied to financial time series, order book data, or other trading-related datasets.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to balance expert knowledge with adaptive learning could be valuable for developing trading strategies that need to combine proven patterns with market adaptation. The selective rollback mechanism provides stability in learning trading rules.
title_cn: MOER：基于专家前缀引导与选择性回滚的混合策略优化
summary_cn: MOER提出一种创新混合策略优化框架，在金融交易领域可实现：1) 专家交易模式引导下的智能体学习 2) 自适应市场探索能力 3) 通过选择性回滚机制确保策略稳定性。该方法特别适用于需结合经典交易策略与市场环境适应的量化场景。

title: Equilibria and Learning in Competitive Market Making
summary: We propose a market-making game played among $N \ge 2$ strategic market makers and a single non-strategic representative trader. In a continuous quote space, standard finite-game arguments do not apply, while non-convex and discontinuous payoffs rule out classical continuous existence results and complicate learning. Nonetheless, we characterize pure-strategy Nash equilibria (PSNEs) and show that at least one PSNE always exists under minimal assumptions on the underlying asset value distribution, and that the equilibrium bid-ask spread widens strictly with asset value volatility. To obtain a tractable learning framework, we discretize prices and, under an additional regularity condition, show that the time-averaged play of no-internal-regret learners approaches the continuous Nash price envelope as the tick size vanishes. Finally, we empirically validate our theoretical results through numerical simulations.
core_methodology: Game-theoretic analysis of competitive market-making with Nash equilibrium characterization and learning algorithms
data_sources: Theoretical market model with simulated data (no real market data used)
alpha_potential: Insights into equilibrium bid-ask spread behavior under volatility, potentially useful for market-making algorithms
title_cn: 竞争性做市中的均衡与学习
summary_cn: 本研究通过博弈论框架分析多个策略性做市商之间的竞争均衡，证明纯策略纳什均衡存在性并揭示价差波动关系。其离散化价格学习方法为算法做市策略开发提供理论支持，适合高频交易场景应用。

title: Harnessing Language Models as Optimization Modeling Agents
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can translate natural-language optimization problems into solver programs, but reliably producing correct formulations and implementations remains challenging. Existing approaches improve optimization modeling through agentic workflows or task-specific post-training. This raises a practical question: can a lightweight harness using a single model role achieve competitive performance without additional training? We introduce OPTICYCLE and OPTISTATE, two lightweight inference harnesses for optimization modeling, and evaluate them on nine benchmarks comprising 2,634 problems using 11 Qwen variants spanning 0.6B-27B parameters. Our results show that execution-guided revision consistently improves macro accuracy over direct generation for all evaluated models, with gains of up to 49.46 percentage points. Despite their simplicity, both harnesses outperform six adapted agentic workflows in same-model comparisons and four evaluated post-trained optimization models at comparable model sizes, without additional training. Explicit formulation state provides further but model-dependent improvements, suggesting that additional structure is not universally beneficial.
core_methodology: Introduces lightweight inference harnesses (OPTICYCLE and OPTISTATE) that use execution-guided revision to improve the accuracy of LLMs in translating natural-language optimization problems into solver programs.
data_sources: Evaluated on nine benchmarks comprising 2,634 optimization problems, using 11 Qwen language model variants ranging from 0.6B to 27B parameters.
alpha_potential: Potential application in portfolio optimization and strategy formulation by leveraging LLMs to translate investment objectives into executable optimization models, improving efficiency and accuracy in quantitative strategy development.
title_cn: 利用语言模型作为优化建模代理
summary_cn: 本文提出两种轻量级推理框架 (OPTICYCLE 和 OPTISTATE)，利用执行引导的修订来提高语言模型将自然语言优化问题转换为求解程序的能力。在量化投资中，该技术可高效将投资目标转化为可执行的优化模型，提升组合优化和策略开发的准确性与效率。

title: Multichoice Modeling: Exploring Decision Configuration Space under Uncertainty
summary: Decision support has become sophisticated at exploring uncertainty, but much less so at representing the architecture of the decision itself. As a result, the decision space is often narrowed before uncertainty is analyzed, leaving interactions among choices and the effects of alternatives they imply largely invisible. This paper introduces multichoice modeling, a framework for making large decision configuration spaces explicit and computationally explorable under uncertainty. Drawing on the logic of rugged landscapes, we conceptualize such problems as contingent performance landscapes, where interdependent choices generate configuration-specific outcomes whose value changes across uncertain futures. The computational framework combines multidimensional decision and uncertainty spaces in a single simulation. Further, variance-based sensitivity analysis is used for identifying influential choices, and conditional distribution analysis for comparing configuration-specific performance profiles. We demonstrate the framework through three case studies: a manufacturing process upgrade, M&A strategy, and mortgage design. By contrasting conventional uncertainty-only analysis with multichoice modeling, the cases show how opening the decision configuration space can reveal unexpected complementarities, near-best configurations with different risk profiles, and strategies that were not apparent as alternatives at the outset.
core_methodology: Multichoice modeling framework for exploring decision configuration spaces under uncertainty, combining decision and uncertainty spaces in simulations with variance-based sensitivity analysis and conditional distribution analysis
data_sources: Case study data (manufacturing, M&A, mortgage design) - methodology could be adapted to financial datasets
alpha_potential: Potential application in portfolio construction strategy optimization by identifying complementary assets and near-optimal configurations with different risk profiles
title_cn: 多选择建模：不确定性下的决策配置空间探索
summary_cn: 本文提出的多选择建模框架可应用于量化投资领域，通过同步分析多维决策空间和不确定性空间，帮助识别资产间的意外互补性，发掘不同风险特征下的近最优组合配置，对投资策略优化具有实用价值。

title: Transformers with CoT Discover Heavy-Ball Acceleration Through Training
summary: Modern transformers often solve complex tasks by generating and refining intermediate reasoning steps. To develop a theoretical understanding of chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, a notable recent study by Huang et al. (2025) viewed transformers as algorithm executors, and showed that when transformers' CoT steps are supervised by a gradient-descent teacher, they can learn to implement gradient descent for in-context weight prediction in linear regression. In this paper, we study the same in-context weight prediction task but ask whether CoT reasoning can go beyond merely imitating the teacher algorithm. We show that, after initial supervision from a gradient-descent teacher, further trajectory-level supervision using the true regression weights leads the model to implement the Heavy-Ball method, thereby achieving acceleration over the original teacher. Notably, this accelerated algorithm emerges without supervision from any Heavy-Ball teacher. Our results provide a concrete theoretical example in which transformer reasoning can discover new algorithms through training, rather than merely imitate the algorithm used for supervision.
core_methodology: Transformers with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning learn to implement the Heavy-Ball optimization method, which is a second-order momentum-based optimization technique, surpassing the initial supervised gradient descent teacher.
data_sources: Theoretical study with synthetic data for linear regression; potential applicability to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The discovered Heavy-Ball acceleration could be leveraged for adaptive momentum strategies in algorithmic trading, potentially improving convergence in dynamic asset allocation or time-series forecasting models. The ability to learn optimization acceleration without explicit supervision suggests potential for developing adaptive momentum-based trading indicators.
title_cn: 基于思维链训练的Transformer发现动量加速算法
summary_cn: 本文研究证明具备思维链推理能力的Transformer模型在训练过程中能自发掌握动量加速优化方法（Heavy-Ball），而无需显式监督。该发现对金融时序预测和自适应动量策略开发具有潜在价值，特别是对构建能自动发现最优收敛速率的量化交易模型提供新思路。

title: What Comes Next and Why: Interpretable Next-Event Prediction with Neuro-Symbolic Rules
summary: In real-world applications, being able to explain why a prediction is made is often as important - if not more so - than achieving high accuracy. However, existing methods for sequential event prediction typically prioritize accuracy at the expense of interpretability. Neuro-symbolic approaches offer a promising direction to improve interpretability by learning symbolic rules, but extending them to next-event prediction is challenging due to the presence of temporal dependencies. We introduce RULES, a neuro-symbolic model that learns sequential rules directly from data, and combine it with a residual network to form RUNES (Rule Network for Event Sequences). RULES accurately recovers ground truth rules from synthetic data and discovers compact, interpretable rule sets on real data. RUNES combines these rules additively with a residual network, achieving competitive accuracy while providing transparent access to active rules and how residuals adjust predictions.
core_methodology: Neuro-symbolic model combining symbolic rule learning with residual networks for sequential event prediction
data_sources: Synthetic and real-world sequential event data (unspecified financial context)
alpha_potential: Could identify interpretable patterns in market event sequences (e.g., order flows, news events) where transparency is required alongside prediction accuracy
title_cn: 接下来会发生什么及原因：基于神经符号规则的可解释性下一事件预测
summary_cn: RUNES模型通过结合符号规则学习与残差网络，为顺序事件提供可解释的高精度预测。在量化交易中，该技术可应用于需要透明决策的市场事件序列分析（如订单流模式或新闻事件链），在保持预测准确性的同时提供规则解释。

title: Constraint Reasoning and Large Language Models Join Forces: Providing Contrastive Explanations for Real-World Optimisation-Based Applications
summary: We focus on optimisation-based Decision Support Systems in real-world applications. In this context, we aim to provide contrastive explanations that answer users' questions about recommendations based on the solution of an optimisation problem, specifically a Mixed-Integer Program (MIP). Addressing this endeavour is crucial to ensure human oversight of the decisions implemented, as required by international guidelines on trustworthy and responsible automated decision-making systems. We propose a novel methodology that combines constraint reasoning techniques and Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate contrastive explanations for optimisation problems encoded as MIPs. Although LLMs have shown impressive capabilities in Natural Language processing, they can produce incorrect answers due to reasoning limitations. To overcome these limitations, we leverage constraint reasoning techniques to distil the information necessary to produce an explanation, which is then passed as input to an LLM as the so-called graph of reasons. Such a graph captures the semantics and the relationships among constraints of the optimisation problem. Results on real-world scheduling domains show that incorporating constraint reasoning improves explanations generated by the LLM. In particular, using the graph of reasons enables the LLM to produce natural-language explanations that include more relevant reasons while reducing errors compared to explanations generated without this structure.
core_methodology: Combines constraint reasoning techniques and Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate contrastive explanations for Mixed-Integer Programs (MIPs), leveraging a graph of reasons structure to enhance LLM accuracy.
data_sources: Optimization problem encodings (Mixed-Integer Programs) from real-world scheduling domains; no specific financial market data mentioned.
alpha_potential: Potential applicability in portfolio optimization scenarios where explaining trade-offs between different asset allocations is crucial. Could enhance transparency in automated trading systems that use MIP-based optimization.
title_cn: 约束推理与大型语言模型联手：为实际优化应用提供对比解释
summary_cn: 该研究结合约束推理技术和大型语言模型(LLM)，为混合整数规划(MIP)优化问题生成对比解释。通过构建'原因图谱'来提升LLM的解释质量，可应用于投资组合优化等需要对复杂约束关系进行解释的金融场景，增强自动化交易系统的可解释性。

title: Reward-Weighted Preference Optimization for Selective Combinatorial Optimization Problems
summary: Reinforcement learning has emerged as an effective approach for combinatorial optimization, but most existing methods focus on problems such as the Travelling Salesperson Problem (TSP) in which all elements must be served. Selective combinatorial optimization problems (SCOPs), including the Orienteering Problem (OP), Prize-Collecting TSP (PCTSP), Stochastic PCTSP and Knapsack Problem (KP), additionally require selecting which elements to include. This selection creates sampled solutions with substantially different objective values, yet standard preference optimization reduces such comparisons to binary rankings and discards the magnitude of these differences. We introduce Reward-Weighted Preference Optimization (RWPO), a pairwise training objective that incorporates reward-gap information into preference learning. For candidate trajectories sampled from the same instance, RWPO weights each preference loss according to the normalized difference in their rewards, assigning greater training emphasis to comparisons that represent larger improvements in solution quality. We further combine RWPO with scale-specific fine-tuning and reward- and likelihood-weighted tilted sampling to adapt trained policies to larger and shifted instance distributions without relying on local-search post-processing. Experiments on the OP, PCTSP, Stochastic PCTSP, and KP show that RWPO consistently improves over unweighted preference optimization and policy-gradient baselines across a wide range of instance sizes. On the OP, the resulting solver exceeds the mean reward of the Compass metaheuristic at scales from 100 to 2,000 nodes. The results demonstrate that preserving reward-gap information can substantially improve preference-based learning for selective combinatorial optimization and support generalization to large-scale instances.
core_methodology: Reward-Weighted Preference Optimization (RWPO) for selective combinatorial optimization problems, incorporating reward-gap information into preference learning and using scale-specific fine-tuning with reward- and likelihood-weighted tilted sampling.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but applicable to datasets for portfolio optimization, asset selection, or capital allocation problems.
alpha_potential: Could potentially be adapted for portfolio construction where selective asset inclusion and exclusion decisions are required, especially in scenarios with many assets and constraints.
title_cn: 基于奖励加权的偏好优化在选择性组合优化问题中的应用
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种奖励加权的偏好优化方法（RWPO），应用于需要选择性元素组合的问题，如资产组合选择。通过整合奖励差距信息，该方法在优化过程中强调质量差异更大的比较，可潜在用于量化投资中的资产筛选和组合构建。

title: Post-Hoc Feature Selection Layer for Neural Networks Interpretability
summary: The interpretability of complex neural networks remains a critical challenge, especially for models already deployed in high-stakes domains. To address this, we adapted the Feature Selection Layer (FSL) to optimize feature weights post-training, a variant we term post-hoc FSL. Our approach reframes the FSL as a lightweight, trainable module that integrates with already frozen pre-trained models on tabular datasets to highlight the features the original model considers most important. This post-hoc FSL learns feature relevance by fine-tuning its weights based on the original model's learned outputs. Crucially, this process is non-invasive, operating without altering the original model's architecture or its learned parameters. We conducted our experiments using both statistical and visual metrics, including accuracy, F1 score, recall, precision, weighted t-SNE and silhouette score, and also analyzed the stability of the post-hoc FSL on high-dimensional synthetic and real-world tabular datasets. We compared the post-hoc FSL feature weighting method using these metrics against the original embedded FSL and other post-hoc interpretability methods, such as Integrated Gradients, Noise Tunnel, DeepLIFT, Gradient SHAP, and Feature Ablation. Experimental results demonstrate that the post-hoc FSL feature weighting method successfully identified relevant features across the different datasets, maintaining the predictive power of the original neural network while enhancing its interpretability.
core_methodology: Post-hoc Feature Selection Layer (FSL) that integrates with frozen pre-trained neural networks to identify and highlight important features without altering the original model's parameters.
data_sources: Tabular datasets, both synthetic and real-world.
alpha_potential: Enhances interpretability of complex models to identify key predictive features in financial data, potentially leading to more robust feature engineering and model refinement.
title_cn: 用于神经网络可解释性的事后特征选择层
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种事后特征选择层（FSL），通过与预训练神经网络集成，在不改变原有模型参数的情况下，识别并突出高重要性特征，适用于金融数据分析以增强模型可解释性和特征发现。

title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity
summary: Automated agentic-system design is typically evaluated on static task suites with immediate scalar rewards. Deployed systems face persistent shift, delayed dependent feedback, correlated component failures, and costly architecture changes. We formalize meta-agent architecture search as sequential incumbent replacement with switching costs and hard risk constraints and introduce Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS). CMAS retrieves archived architectures and proposes typed graph edits, then scores each against the incumbent by paired shadow replay under common random numbers, with interventional component credit. Promotion requires an empirically calibrated, variance-penalized simultaneous score above a pre-specified margin, and is followed by a simulated canary stage and pre-specified rollback. Since backtests cannot certify meta-level skill, we introduce MetaInvest-Bench, a regime-switching simulator whose specified worker competence makes a surrogate-optimal architecture computable, with leakage-controlled replay, adversarial governance tracks, and five negative controls. Financial streams serve as a risk-sensitive testbed for meta-level generalization; we claim no alpha. Across 96 streams, CMAS cuts normalized mean surrogate dynamic-oracle regret from 0.116 to 0.104 and raises held-out utility from 0.44 to 0.48 over the strongest adaptive baseline; when extra workers add no value, it contracts to near-single-agent teams. Its deployment inference cost is ~6% lower, though its search-inclusive token cost is the highest of the methods compared. The observed per-update false-promotion rate is 3.4% against a nominal 5% target, and 4.8% in a sealed rerun. The calibration is empirical: it concerns an update-level replay statistic on an author-designed benchmark, and guarantees neither full-utility improvement, nor absence of simulated canary-stage harm, nor sequence-level error control.
core_methodology: Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS) for architecture adaptation in non-stationary environments, using archived architectures, typed graph edits, and paired shadow replay under common random numbers with interventional component credit
data_sources: Financial streams as a risk-sensitive testbed, though the paper claims no alpha
alpha_potential: Moderate potential for adaptive systems in dynamic market conditions, but requires further testing on financial data to confirm
title_cn: 保守型元代理搜索：非平稳性下的架构适配
summary_cn: 本文提出一种保守型元代理架构搜索方法(CMAS)，通过档案架构检索和类型化图编辑实现非平稳环境下的系统优化。该方法在96个金融数据流测试中表现优于基准，但需进一步验证其量化交易中的实际应用价值

title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
summary: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.
core_methodology: Transformer-based neural network (OCFormer) for solving high-dimensional optimal control problems in real-time multi-agent path planning, incorporating physics-informed training and permutation equivariance.
data_sources: Simulated multi-agent navigation scenarios with varying initial and final configurations in 2D and 3D environments.
alpha_potential: Potential applications in algorithmic trading for optimizing execution strategies that involve multiple interacting orders or agents in limit order books, especially in high-frequency or multi-asset trading scenarios. The amortized inference capability could help in real-time trading decisions.
title_cn: 基于Transformer的实时多智能体路径规划方法：可变初始/终止条件
summary_cn: 该研究提出OCFormer，一种基于Transformer的神经网络，用于解决多智能体实时路径规划问题。通过物理信息损失函数训练，该模型可快速生成最优轨迹，适用于高频交易中多订单执行的实时优化。其轻量级迁移学习框架还能快速适应市场变化。

title: Continuous-depth Deep Gaussian Processes
summary: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are appealing Bayesian regression models, but their standard discrete-depth parameterization often becomes harder to optimize as depth grows. We argue that depth is better treated as a latent continuous evolution than as a long discrete stack. We therefore propose a continuous-depth formulation in which the latent representation follows a stochastic differential equation with a depth-indexed drift family equipped with a GP-based prior. This reframes the core design choice as the prior placed on that family, rather than adopting a purely neural continuous-depth parameterization as in neural ODE or neural SDE models. We study two instantiations of this idea: CDGP, a direct GP prior over the state--depth drift, and FlowDGP, a flow-evolved prior that captures richer depth dependence at lower training cost. To motivate the redesign, we analyze how the single-sample DGP objective can become increasingly sensitive under repeated layer composition, while residual DGP is a useful first repair that still remains a finite discrete construction. We also give pathwise sensitivity analysis for the continuous-depth formulation. Experiments on synthetic, benchmark, and large-scale regression tasks show that residual DGP improves over plain DGP, while CDGP and FlowDGP provide a stronger overall story across the regimes we study.
core_methodology: Continuous-depth formulation of Gaussian Processes using stochastic differential equations with depth-indexed drift families, particularly CDGP and FlowDGP variants
data_sources: Synthetic, benchmark, and large-scale regression datasets (paper doesn't specify financial data but methodology is transferable)
alpha_potential: Potential for detecting nonlinear market patterns and regime shifts through continuous-depth probabilistic modeling, especially in volatility modeling and curve fitting
title_cn: 连续深度深度高斯过程
summary_cn: 该研究提出的连续深度高斯过程(CDGP/FlowDGP)通过随机微分方程建模深度演化过程，相比传统离散层叠结构更适合捕捉金融市场中的非线性连续动态（如波动率曲面或期限结构演化）。其贝叶斯特性对于量化不确定性和防范过拟合具有天然优势，在衍生品定价、风险因子建模等领域具备应用潜力。

title: GateFormer: Forecast-Space Decomposition for Intra-Hour Solar Irradiance Prediction from Sky Images
summary: Sub-hourly dispatch, balancing, and storage control increasingly depend on forecasts that anticipate rapid variability in solar generation. Accurate sky-image-based irradiance forecasting requires a combination of visual cloud dynamics with recent irradiance state while adapting to different short-term irradiance-change regimes. To address this, we introduce GateFormer, a GHI-conditioned dual-decoder ViT for intra-hour global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting through forecast-space decomposition. GateFormer embeds observed GHI into the visual token stream, allowing interaction with sky-image patch features through self-attention. From this shared representation, a Trajectory Head predicts future GHI sequence, while a Delta Head predicts final-horizon change from the latest observed GHI. The two final-horizon forecasts are adaptively weighted in prediction space, with magnitude- and direction-supervision targeting the remaining error. On the NREL-TSI benchmark, GateFormer attains 125.01 W/m^2 RMSE at +30 min, improving over a state-of-the-art transformer baseline by 9.6% under paired-timestamp evaluation. Across NREL-TSI, Chilbolton, and SIRTA, GateFormer achieves the lowest final-horizon RMSE among the evaluated baselines, with forecast skill of 22.97-28.86% relative to smart persistence. Component ablations show adaptive weighting outperforms both individual decoders and fixed averaging, distinguishing GateFormer from conventional forecast combination, while the supervised correction further reduces RMSE by 1.68 W/m^2 and MAE by 4.86 W/m^2. Ramp-regime diagnostics show larger gains during operationally important positive ramps, reducing RMSE by 26.27 W/m^2. These results identify forecast-space decomposition as an alternative forecasting formulation, with potential relevance to other multimodal short-horizon forecasting tasks and deployment using only sky images and measured GHI.
core_methodology: GateFormer utilizes a GHI-conditioned dual-decoder Vision Transformer (ViT) for intra-hour global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting. It combines visual cloud dynamics from sky images with recent irradiance data through self-attention mechanisms, and decomposes the forecast into trajectory and delta components with adaptive weighting.
data_sources: Sky images and measured Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) data from datasets like NREL-TSI, Chilbolton, and SIRTA.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for predicting solar energy generation, which is relevant for trading in energy markets, particularly for renewable energy derivatives or grid balancing services. The ability to forecast rapid variability in solar generation could provide an edge in markets sensitive to short-term energy supply fluctuations.
title_cn: GateFormer：基于预测空间分解的天空图像太阳辐射强度小时内预测
summary_cn: GateFormer采用GHI条件化的双解码器ViT模型，通过天空图像和实测辐射数据，结合视觉云动态和自注意力机制，实现小时内太阳辐射强度预测。其预测空间分解和自适应加权方法在可再生能源市场的短期交易中具有潜在应用价值，特别是在电力衍生品和电网平衡服务中。

title: Nonparametric autoregressive estimation of probability distributions with parallel gradient boosting
summary: Nonparametric estimation of joint probability distributions is a core problem in statistics, which is notoriously challenging with high-dimensional data. Such challenges also arise with conditional distribution estimation and have led to flexible algorithms that aim to tackle the ''curse of dimensionality'' by exploiting predictive structures of lower dimension than the ambient space. In this paper, we study the use of such conditional distribution estimators to estimate joint distributions by factorizing the latter in an ''autoregressive'' way. We show that for loss functions satisfying a subadditivity property, bounds on the convergence rate of an autoregressive estimator can be derived from bounds on the convergence rate of the conditional distribution estimators. These bounds relate the difficulty of estimating the joint distribution to that of estimating the most challenging factor in the autoregressive factorization. When the conditional estimators adapt to sparsity in their conditioning sets, we characterize this difficulty through variable elimination in an undirected dependence graph. This allows bounding the rates of convergence by quantities related to the sparsity of the graph, and provides an additional motivation for the autoregressive approach.
