We then evaluate the practical performance of an autoregressive estimator based on parallel gradient boosting, a flexible nonparametric method for estimating conditional distributions. The estimator demonstrates competitive estimation performance on various simulated and real datasets, even without optimizing the factorization order. Together, these results support nonparametric autoregressive estimation as a practical approach to flexible joint distribution estimation.
core_methodology: Nonparametric autoregressive estimation of joint probability distributions using parallel gradient boosting for conditional distribution estimation, which adapts to sparsity in conditioning sets.
data_sources: Simulated and real datasets (specifics not detailed in abstract, but could include financial time series data).
alpha_potential: Potential for improved modeling of complex, high-dimensional financial data dependencies, which could enhance risk assessment, portfolio optimization, and predictive modeling in trading strategies.
title_cn: 基于并行梯度提升的非参数自回归概率分布估计
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种非参数自回归方法，利用并行梯度提升估计联合概率分布。通过适应条件集的稀疏性，该方法在复杂高维数据中显示出竞争力，可潜在提升金融时间序列建模，助力量化交易中的风险评估和投资组合优化。

title: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)
summary: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training. By casting the values and derivatives at the query and neighbouring samples as latent variables in a constrained optimisation problem, the burden of long training loops becomes one of on-demand local solves. We establish Diona's theoretical properties including finite-sample coverage and, in the noiseless case, convergence to the true state and derivatives under dense sampling. In a nonlinear regression benchmark on six functions of three to eight dimensions, Diona was more accurate than a Gaussian process (GP) on noiseless data especially with denser data sets. Furthermore, as with GP, it produced uncertainty bounds that contained the true value at more than 95% of query points in four functions. Diona's time to a first prediction after a data set update was three to four orders of magnitude shorter than that of the GP, and two to three orders shorter than that of a neural network, which was more accurate but offers no uncertainty quantification. This low latency is paid for by on-demand predictions, so this latency advantage applies when relatively few predictions are needed between data updates.
core_methodology: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) is a regression method that estimates the state and its derivatives at a query point along with admissible bounds without requiring long global training. It uses constrained optimization to handle values and derivatives at query and neighboring samples as latent variables, enabling on-demand local solves.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but applicable to any quantitative financial dataset where regression on state and derivatives is required, such as price series, volatility surfaces, or factor models.
alpha_potential: Potential applications in high-frequency trading and real-time risk management due to low latency in predictions and uncertainty quantification, which could be leveraged for dynamic portfolio adjustments and real-time signal generation.
title_cn: 直接推理在容许集上的方法（Diona）
summary_cn: Diona是一种新的回归方法，通过将查询点及其邻近样本的值和导数作为潜在变量进行约束优化，直接利用样本估计查询点的状态及其导数以及容许边界。相比高斯过程，它具有更低的延迟，适用于需要快速预测和高频数据更新的金融应用，如高频交易和实时风险管理。

title: Multi-View Causal Discovery without Non-Gaussianity: Identifiability and Algorithms
summary: Causal discovery is a difficult problem that typically relies on strong assumptions on the data-generating model, such as non-Gaussianity. In practice, many modern applications provide multiple related views of the same system, which has rarely been considered for causal discovery. Here, we leverage this multi-view structure to achieve causal discovery with weak assumptions. We propose a multi-view linear Structural Equation Model (SEM) that extends the well-known framework of non-Gaussian disturbances by alternatively leveraging correlation over views. We prove the identifiability of the model for acyclic SEMs. Subsequently, we propose several multi-view causal discovery algorithms, inspired by single-view algorithms (DirectLiNGAM, PairwiseLiNGAM, and ICA-LiNGAM). The new methods are validated through simulations and applications on neuroimaging data, where they enable the estimation of causal graphs between brain regions.
core_methodology: Multi-view linear Structural Equation Model (SEM) for causal discovery that leverages correlation across multiple views of the same system, extending the non-Gaussian disturbances framework.
data_sources: Neuroimaging data in the paper, but can be adapted to multiple financial data sources (e.g., price, volume, order book data from different exchanges).
alpha_potential: Potential to identify causal relationships between different market signals or factors, which could be used to predict asset movements or understand market dynamics.
title_cn: 无需非高斯性的多视图因果发现：可识别性与算法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种多视图线性结构方程模型（SEM），利用多个相关视图的弱假设实现因果发现。该框架可应用于金融市场，通过分析不同数据源（如价格、成交量）之间的因果关系，挖掘市场动态中的有效信号。适用于构建因果驱动的交易策略。

title: Agent-Environment Alignment via Automated Interface Generation
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown impressive reasoning capabilities in interactive decision-making tasks. These agents interact with environment through intermediate interfaces, such as predefined action spaces and interaction rules, which mediate the perception and action. However, mismatches often happen between the internal expectations of the agent regarding the influence of its issued actions and the actual state transitions in the environment, a phenomenon referred to as agent-environment misalignment. While prior work has invested substantially in improving agent strategies and environment design, the critical role of the interface still remains underexplored. In this work, we empirically demonstrate that agent-environment misalignment poses a significant bottleneck to agent performance. To mitigate this issue, we propose ALIGN, an Auto-Aligned Interface Generation framework that alleviates the misalignment by enriching the interface. Specifically, the ALIGN-generated interface enhances both the static information of the environment and the step-wise observations returned to the agent. Implemented as a lightweight wrapper, this interface achieves the alignment without modifying either the agent logic or the environment code. Experiments across multiple domains including embodied tasks, web navigation and tool-use, show consistent performance improvements, with up to a 45.67% success rate improvement observed in ALFWorld. Meanwhile, ALIGN-generated interface can generalize across different agent architectures and LLM backbones without interface regeneration. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/THUNLP-MT/ALIGN.
core_methodology: Proposes ALIGN, an Auto-Aligned Interface Generation framework that enhances agent-environment interaction by enriching the interface between LLM agents and environments without modifying agent logic or environment code
data_sources: Experimental results across multiple domains including embodied tasks, web navigation and tool-use (specifically ALFWorld benchmark environment)
alpha_potential: Potential to improve LLM-based trading agent performance by reducing agent-environment misalignment in financial market interactions, particularly in complex, multi-step decision-making scenarios
title_cn: 通过自动界面生成实现智能体与环境对齐
summary_cn: 本文提出的ALIGN框架通过优化LLM智能体与交易环境间的交互界面，显著提升决策准确性。在金融交易场景中，该技术可减少交易信号与市场实际响应间的偏差，尤其适用于多步骤高频交易策略的自动化执行，实验显示最高可提升45%任务成功率。其接口设计兼容不同智能体架构，为量化交易系统提供灵活的智能体部署方案。

title: To Distill or Decide? Understanding the Algorithmic Trade-off in Partially Observable Reinforcement Learning
summary: Partial observability is a notorious challenge in reinforcement learning (RL), due to the need to learn complex, history-dependent policies. Recent empirical successes have used privileged expert distillation--which leverages availability of latent state information during training (e.g., from a simulator) to learn and imitate the optimal latent, Markovian policy--to disentangle the task of "learning to see" from "learning to act". While expert distillation is more computationally efficient than RL without latent state information, it also has well-documented failure modes. In this paper--through a simple but instructive theoretical model called the perturbed Block MDP, and controlled experiments on challenging simulated locomotion tasks--we investigate the algorithmic trade-off between privileged expert distillation and standard RL without privileged information. Our main findings are: (1) The trade-off empirically hinges on the stochasticity of the latent dynamics, as theoretically predicted by contrasting approximate decodability with belief contraction in the perturbed Block MDP; and (2) The optimal latent policy is not always the best latent policy to distill. Our results suggest new guidelines for effectively exploiting privileged information, potentially advancing the efficiency of policy learning across many practical partially observable domains.
core_methodology: Investigates algorithmic trade-offs between privileged expert distillation (using latent state information during training) and standard RL in partially observable environments, with theoretical modeling and controlled experiments.
data_sources: Simulated environments and locomotion tasks (no real market data used in study)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving reinforcement learning approaches to trading in partially observable market conditions, though requires adaptation to financial datasets
title_cn: 蒸馏还是决策？理解部分可观测强化学习中的算法权衡
summary_cn: 本研究通过扰动块MDP理论模型和模拟实验，分析了在部分可观测环境下的两种强化学习策略：特权专家蒸馏与标准RL的算法权衡。发现潜在动态的随机性直接影响策略效果，且最优潜在策略并不总是最佳蒸馏对象。这些发现为金融交易中的部分可观测问题处理提供了新思路，尤其适用于需要历史依赖决策的量化交易场景。

title: Near-Optimal Regret for KL-Regularized Multi-Armed Bandits
summary: Recent studies have shown that reinforcement learning with KL-regularized objectives can enjoy faster rates of convergence or logarithmic regret, in contrast to the classical $\sqrt{T}$-type regret in the unregularized setting. However, the statistical efficiency of online learning with respect to KL-regularized objectives remains far from completely characterized, even when specialized to multi-armed bandits (MABs). We address this problem for MABs via a sharp analysis of KL-UCB using a novel peeling argument, which yields a $\tilde{O}(\eta K\log^2T)$ upper bound: the first high-probability regret bound with linear dependence on $K$. Here, $T$ is the time horizon, $K$ is the number of arms, $\eta^{-1}$ is the regularization intensity, and $\tilde{O}$ hides all logarithmic factors except those involving $\log T$. The near-tightness of our analysis is certified by the first non-constant lower bound $\Omega(\eta K \log T)$, which follows from subtle hard-instance constructions and a tailored decomposition of the Bayes prior. Moreover, in the low-regularization regime (i.e., large $\eta$), we show that the KL-regularized regret for MABs is $\eta$-independent and scales as $\tilde{\Theta}(\sqrt{KT})$. Overall, our results provide a thorough understanding of KL-regularized MABs across all regimes of $\eta$ and yield nearly optimal bounds in terms of $K$, $\eta$, and $T$.
core_methodology: The paper presents an analysis of KL-regularized multi-armed bandits (MABs) using a novel peeling argument and provides near-optimal regret bounds. The methodology focuses on reinforcement learning with KL-regularized objectives, which can lead to faster convergence rates and logarithmic regret.
data_sources: The paper does not specify specific market data sources, as it is theoretical in nature. However, the methodology could be applied to financial data such as stock prices, trading volumes, or other market indicators.
alpha_potential: The KL-regularized approach could potentially be adapted for trading strategies that require efficient exploration-exploitation trade-offs, such as dynamic asset allocation or algorithmic trading. The improved regret bounds suggest better performance in scenarios where traditional MAB algorithms might underperform.
title_cn: KL正则化多臂老虎机的接近最优遗憾
summary_cn: 本研究通过KL正则化多臂老虎机（MAB）的锐利分析，提出了接近最优的遗憾上界。这一方法在强化学习中展示了更快的收敛速度和更低的遗憾，适用于需要高效探索-利用权衡的金融场景，如动态资产配置和算法交易。其理论成果为实际交易策略的优化提供了潜在的理论基础。

title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to long-horizon tasks such as scientific discovery and machine learning engineering (MLE), where sustained self-evolution becomes a key capability. However, existing MLE agents suffer from isolated exploration, inefficient experience reuse, and lack of hierarchical control, which together hinder long-horizon optimization. We present MLEvolve, an LLM-based self-evolving multi-agent framework for end-to-end machine learning algorithm discovery. By extending tree search to Progressive MCGS, MLEvolve enables cross-branch information flow through graph-based reference edges and gradually shifts the search from broad exploration to focused exploitation with an entropy-inspired progressive schedule. To allow the agent to evolve with accumulated experience, we introduce Retrospective Memory, which combines a cold-start domain knowledge base with a dynamic global memory for task-specific experience retrieval and reuse. For stable long-horizon iteration, we further decouple strategic planning from code generation with adaptive coding modes. Evaluation on MLE-Bench shows that MLEvolve achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple dimensions including average medal rate and valid submission rate under a 12-hour budget (half the standard runtime). Moreover, MLEvolve also outperforms specialized algorithm discovery methods including AlphaEvolve on mathematical algorithm optimization tasks, demonstrating strong cross-domain generalization. Code is available at https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve.
core_methodology: LLM-based self-evolving multi-agent framework with Progressive MCGS tree search for machine learning algorithm discovery, featuring cross-branch information flow and dynamic experience reuse through Retrospective Memory
data_sources: Primarily designed for general machine learning algorithm discovery, not specific financial data (but adaptable to structured market data)
alpha_potential: Potential for systematic discovery of novel ML architectures for trading strategies. The self-evolving nature could uncover non-obvious feature combinations or trading rules through long-horizon optimization
title_cn: MLEvolve：用于自动化机器学习算法发现的自进化框架
summary_cn: 本研究提出的MLEvolve自进化多智能体框架通过渐进式蒙特卡洛树搜索和动态记忆机制，可实现机器算法长期迭代优化。该系统在算法探索与经验复用方面表现出色，经适当改造后可用于量化策略的自动化发现与持续优化，特别是对于多因子组合或高频交易策略的演进式开发具有潜在应用价值。

title: CollabFlow: Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Collaboration
summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) lets a system improve from its own outcomes; in LLM-based multi-agent systems, Agents refine one another within a task, and outcomes improve how they collaborate across tasks. However, existing multi-agent collaboration leaves this loop open: collaboration is pre-defined at the operator level, topology-only learning keeps verbatim exchange that propagates errors, and reward maximization on a system's own outcomes concentrates on a few teams. To address these challenges, we propose CollabFlow, an RSI system of Learned Agent Collaboration: a trainable Collab-Director constructs teams of complete Agents, a frozen executor runs them, and each round's outcomes retrain the director. Within each round, the edges of a collaboration graph carry protocols of Evidence-Conditioned Communication: a receiver adopts a differing answer only when the sender's evidence is stronger by a margin, so the director learns who communicates and how. Across rounds, we further propose Collaborative Trajectory Balance (CTB), a flow-based objective that credits each team once across its construction orders and targets a reward-proportional distribution over teams, so several good teams stay in play. We also bound how far this self-generated target moves between rounds, which shrinks as records accumulate. On twelve datasets, CollabFlow outperforms all baselines and keeps improving across rounds. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CollabFlow-631E.
core_methodology: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) system for multi-agent collaboration, utilizing Evidence-Conditioned Communication and Collaborative Trajectory Balance (CTB) to optimize agent teams and their interactions.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but likely involves synthetic or benchmark datasets given the reference to twelve datasets in evaluations.
alpha_potential: Potential to optimize trading strategies by dynamically improving agent collaboration, possibly enhancing signal generation, risk management, or execution algorithms through iterative learning.
title_cn: CollabFlow：代理协作的递归自我优化
summary_cn: CollabFlow提出了一种递归自我改进的代理协作系统，通过证据条件通信和协作轨迹平衡优化多代理团队的合作，适用于动态交易策略优化和提高执行算法效率。

title: Redundancy Meets Synergy: Dependency-aware Expert Selection for MoE via Submodular Optimization
summary: While Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models effectively scale model capacity through sparse activation, their deployment is often bottlenecked by prohibitive memory requirements. Extracting a compact subset of experts presents a promising solution. However, existing expert selection heuristics predominantly rely on Top-$k$ ranking, which isolates the evaluation of individual experts and ignores the intricate inter-expert dependencies introduced by the MoE gating network. In this paper, we propose DS-MoE, a theoretically grounded framework that redefines expert selection via difference-of-submodular (DS) optimization. By analyzing the second-order Taylor expansion of the loss degradation, we reveal functional duality within expert combinations: redundancy (where experts encode overlapping representations) and synergy (where experts provide complementary error cancellation). To navigate this duality, we mathematically decouple redundancy reduction from synergy maximization by formulating the selection objective as a DS function. Furthermore, we devise a tailored majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm with provable guarantees to efficiently identify a high-quality expert subset. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DS-MoE effectively preserves indispensable expert combinations, achieving superior performance compared to the state-of-the-art baselines.
core_methodology: Difference-of-submodular (DS) optimization for expert selection in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, focusing on redundancy reduction and synergy maximization in expert combinations.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but applicable to various ML model deployment scenarios, potentially including financial data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could enhance model efficiency in trading strategies by optimizing expert selection in MoE models, potentially leading to more accurate predictions and better resource utilization.
title_cn: 冗余与协同：基于次模优化的MoE专家选择依赖性研究
summary_cn: 本文提出的DS-MoE框架通过冗余减少和协同最大化来优化MoE模型中的专家选择，可提升交易策略中预测模型的效率和准确性，具有潜在的应用价值。

title: Diffusion-Based Hypothesis Testing and Change-Point Detection
summary: Score-based methods have recently seen increasing popularity in modeling and generation. Methods have been constructed to perform hypothesis testing and change-point detection with score functions, but these methods are in general not as powerful as their likelihood-based peers. Recent works consider generalizing the score-based Fisher divergence into a diffusion-divergence by transforming score functions via multiplication with a matrix-valued function or a weight matrix. In this paper, we extend the score-based hypothesis test and change-point detection stopping rule into their diffusion-based analogs. Additionally, we theoretically quantify the performance of these diffusion-based algorithms and study scenarios where optimal performance is achievable. We propose a method of numerically optimizing the weight matrix and present numerical simulations to illustrate the advantages of diffusion-based algorithms.
core_methodology: Diffusion-based hypothesis testing and change-point detection algorithms enhanced through optimized weight matrices
data_sources: General time-series data (not market-specific in paper but applicable to financial series)
alpha_potential: Potential for detecting regime changes in financial markets and identifying structural breaks in price series/volatility
title_cn: 基于扩散模型的假设检验与变点检测
summary_cn: 本文提出的扩散式变点检测算法可优化金融市场中的结构突变识别，通过权重矩阵优化提升传统得分函数方法的统计功效，适用于波动率突变检测、市场状态转换识别等量化交易场景。

title: On the Gradient Domination of the LQG Problem
summary: We consider solutions to the linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) regulator problem via policy gradient (PG) methods. Although PG methods have demonstrated strong theoretical guarantees in solving the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem, despite its nonconvex landscape, their theoretical understanding in the LQG setting remains limited. Notably, the LQG problem lacks gradient dominance in the classical parameterization, i.e., with a dynamic controller, which hinders global convergence guarantees. In this work, we study a PG method for the LQG problem by adopting an alternative parameterization of the set of stabilizing controllers and employing a lifting argument. We refer to this parameterization as a history representation of the control input as it is parameterized by past input and output data from the previous p time-steps. Under this parameterization, the infinite-history LQG optimization reduces to an equivalent static state-feedback LQR problem, allowing us to recover gradient dominance and smoothness. For finite history length p, we establish model-based and model-free convergence guarantees up to a geometrically decaying history-truncation error.
core_methodology: The paper explores policy gradient methods for solving the linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) regulator problem by adopting an alternative parameterization of stabilizing controllers. This approach converts the LQG problem into an equivalent static state-feedback LQR problem, enabling gradient dominance and smoothness.
data_sources: The methodology is theoretical and does not explicitly use financial data, but it could be adapted for use with market data in trading applications.
alpha_potential: This approach could be adapted for portfolio optimization and dynamic asset allocation, potentially providing a systematic way to adjust trading strategies based on past performance and market conditions.
title_cn: 论LQG问题的梯度支配性
summary_cn: 本文通过采用稳定控制器的替代参数化方法，研究了线性二次高斯（LQG）调节器问题的策略梯度解决途径。该方法将LQG问题转化为等效的静态状态反馈LQR问题，适用于动态调整交易策略，可能为组合优化提供一个系统性框架。

title: Stochastic Matching Bandits with Rare Optimization Updates
summary: We introduce a bandit framework for stochastic matching under the multinomial logit (MNL) choice model. In this setting, $N$ agents on one side are assigned to $K$ arms on the other side, where each arm stochastically selects an agent from its assigned pool according to unknown preferences and yields a corresponding reward over a horizon $T$. The objective is to minimize regret by maximizing the cumulative revenue from successful matches. A naive approach requires solving an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem at every round, resulting in a prohibitive computational cost. To address this challenge, we propose batched algorithms that strategically limit the number of times matching assignments are updated to $\Theta(\log\log T)$ over the entire horizon. By invoking expensive combinatorial optimization only on a vanishing fraction of rounds, our algorithms substantially reduce overall computational overhead while still achieving a regret bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{T})$.
core_methodology: The paper proposes batched algorithms for stochastic matching problems under the multinomial logit (MNL) choice model. The approach reduces computational overhead by limiting matching assignment updates to Θ(log log T) over the horizon, using combinatorial optimization sparingly while achieving a regret bound of Õ(√T).
data_sources: No specific financial data sources are mentioned in the abstract, but the framework could theoretically be applied to market data where matching problems arise (e.g., order book matching, broker-client matching).
alpha_potential: Potential exists in matching optimization problems in finance (e.g., portfolio allocation strategies, client-broker matching systems, dark pool liquidity matching) where minimizing regret while maintaining computational efficiency is valuable.
title_cn: 具有罕见优化更新的随机匹配多臂老虎机
summary_cn: 本文提出一种针对多项式Logit选择模型的批处理算法，通过将匹配更新次数限制为Θ(log log T)来显著降低计算成本，同时保持Õ(√T)的遗憾界。此方法可应用于金融市场中的匹配优化问题，如订单匹配或流动性分配，在保证计算效率的同时优化匹配收益。

title: Parallel gradient boosting for flexible estimation of conditional distributions
summary: Boosting is one of the most successful learning techniques for standard classification and regression tasks. Its extension to multi-output prediction problems has found an increasing number of applications in recent years. Among them is the prediction of entire conditional distributions rather than single functionals, which can often be framed as a multi-output regression problem, for example multiple quantile regression. Addressing such problems with classical implementations of boosting is computationally challenging, because usually one base model is trained for each target at every iteration. More efficient variants of boosting have been proposed to speed up training, but they tend to be tied to specific loss functions and classes of base learners, usually decision trees. In this work, we study a modification of the gradient boosting algorithm, which we call parallel gradient boosting, designed to circumvent all these limitations. The core idea is to use a common descent direction for all training observations. By doing so, only one base model is needed at each iteration, regardless of the number of targets, which allows for considerable performance gains. We establish sufficient conditions for the convergence of the algorithm, whose practical use is introduced via the multiple quantile regression setting. We show that in such a setting, it provides predictions of similar quality to state-of-the-art boosting libraries such as XGBoost, while being faster by several orders of magnitude. Then, we evaluate the properties of the resulting conditional distribution estimator, which is shown empirically to outperform other nonparametric and semiparametric estimators, especially in high-dimensional settings and in the presence of mixed and/or missing covariates.
core_methodology: Parallel gradient boosting for efficient estimation of conditional distributions via multiple quantile regression, using a common descent direction for all training observations to reduce computational complexity.
data_sources: Generic high-dimensional data with mixed/missing covariates, applicable to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: Potential for more efficient estimation of conditional asset return distributions, particularly useful for risk management and quantile-based trading strategies. Improved speed could enable real-time applications.
title_cn: 并行梯度提升算法在条件分布灵活估计中的应用
summary_cn: 该研究提出的并行梯度提升算法通过优化多目标回归中的共同下降方向，显著提高了条件分布估计的效率。其在高维金融数据场景下的性能优势，特别适用于实时分位数回归策略开发和风险价值(VaR)计算等量化交易应用。

title: Reinforcement Learning and Operational Research: A Review of Methodological Integration and Research Directions
summary: The growing demand for real-time, data-driven decision-making in complex and dynamic systems is placing increasing pressure on Operational Research (OR) methodologies. Sequential decision-making under uncertainty has long been studied in OR through Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, and their approximations, and reinforcement learning (RL) provides simulation-based methods for learning decision policies in such problems. Recent research shows an increasing interest in integrating RL with OR to address dynamic decision-making problems and enhance heuristic and exact methods for combinatorial optimization. The overarching goal across these efforts is to improve solution quality, computational efficiency, and robustness. Given the diversity of integration approaches and application settings, there is a clear need for a systematic and technically detailed review of how RL empowers OR methods. To address this gap, this paper presents a structured review of two methodological roles of RL in OR. The first concerns sequential decision problems in dynamic environments, where states evolve and decisions are repeated over time. The second concerns static combinatorial optimization problems, where inputs are fixed before the solution process begins and RL either constructs solutions or supports heuristic and exact algorithms. Digital twins provide an optional deployment and evaluation layer for training, testing, and validating these methods. We critically synthesize recent advances across these roles and uses, highlighting their advantages, implementation requirements, limitations, and challenges. Finally, we consolidate guidance on when the reviewed approaches may be considered and outline directions for future research on the methodological and practical integration of RL and OR.
core_methodology: Reinforcement learning applied to sequential decision-making and combinatorial optimization problems in operational research
data_sources: Simulated or real-world operational scenarios, potentially including financial data for dynamic decision-making
alpha_potential: Potential for enhancing decision-making in dynamic and uncertain environments, applicable to algorithmic trading and portfolio optimization
title_cn: 强化学习与运筹学：方法整合与研究方向的综述
summary_cn: 本文探讨了强化学习与运筹学的整合，特别是在动态不确定环境下的顺序决策和组合优化问题中的应用。这对于高频交易、投资组合优化等金融领域具有潜在的理论价值。

title: Dynamics of the Liquidity Profile in Concentrated Liquidity Provision: An SPIDE Approach
summary: We model the dynamics of the liquidity profile in Uniswap~V3 and other concentrated-liquidity automated market makers with a stochastic partial integro-differential equation (SPIDE). The profile, the aggregate of all provider positions across tick space, evolves under a degenerate Sturm--Liouville operator, which encodes mean-reverting concentration around the market price, coupled with a Hilbert--Schmidt integral operator, which captures nonlocal redistribution driven by provider repositioning. We establish existence and uniqueness of the mild solution in a weighted $L^2$ space built on the Gegenbauer eigensystem, and reduce the SPIDE to a coupled system of linear stochastic differential equations whose low-order modes describe the level, slope, and curvature of the profile. Pairing the SPIDE with a log-price process yields tractable expressions for pool reserves, pool value, and loss-versus-rebalancing under Ornstein--Uhlenbeck-type and Black--Scholes-type noise. A finite-rank calibration in a fixed reference frame, applied to three Uniswap pools, gives interpretable estimates and lowers active-band forecast error relative to a martingale benchmark on the two pools compatible with the stationary specification. On the third pool, out-of-sample diagnostics are consistent with nonstationarity, which motivates price-aware and time-varying extensions.
core_methodology: Stochastic partial integro-differential equation (SPIDE) approach to model liquidity profile dynamics in concentrated-liquidity AMMs like Uniswap V3, reduced to a system of linear stochastic differential equations
data_sources: Uniswap V3 pools (three specific pools mentioned in the abstract)
alpha_potential: Provides framework for forecasting liquidity profile changes and potential arbitrage opportunities in concentrated-liquidity pools, particularly through active-band forecasting and state-dependent modeling
title_cn: 集中流动性提供中的流动性分布动态：一种SPIDE方法
summary_cn: 本研究通过随机偏积分微分方程(SPIDE)建立Uniswap V3等集中流动性AMM的流动性分布动态模型，将复杂系统简化为线性随机微分方程。在三个Uniswap资金池的实证表明，该方法能降低活跃带预测误差，并为价格感知型流动性调整提供理论基础，对DeFi套利和做市策略具有应用价值。

title: Equilibrium in closed constant-function market maker economies
summary: We study equilibria in a closed, fee-free constant-function market maker (CFMM) economy with two assets and two agents. An interior state is a unilateral no-trade equilibrium exactly when the CFMM marginal price equals both agents' marginal rates of substitution. For an interior initial state, individually rational unilateral equilibria are Pareto optimal relative to the fixed CFMM invariant. A weak representative agent is obtained at each fixed equilibrium by weighted sup-convolution, whereas, under some regularity assumptions, a state-independent strong representative agent exists exactly when agents share the same homothetic preference. Every interior feasible state is reachable through finitely many valid trades, but an individually rational interior target need not be improvement reachable. Alternating utility-maximizing trades converge to a Pareto optimal unilateral equilibrium.
core_methodology: Analysis of equilibrium conditions in fee-free constant-function market maker (CFMM) systems with two assets and two agents, focusing on Pareto optimality and trade convergence properties.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any two-asset CFMM system (e.g., Uniswap-like pools) with rational agents.
alpha_potential: Provides theoretical foundation for predicting price stability and optimal trade routing in decentralized exchanges, with implications for arbitrage strategies and liquidity provision optimization.
title_cn: 封闭式恒定函数做市商经济中的均衡研究
summary_cn: 本研究建立了无手续费的二元资产CFMM系统均衡理论，揭示了当边际价格与代理人的边际替代率一致时达到帕累托最优。成果可用于优化去中心化交易所的套利策略设计，并预测流动性池的价格收敛行为。

title: Bayesian Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with Abstention
summary: We study the Bayesian fixed-confidence best-arm identification problem in which a learner can abstain from making a terminal recommendation. Subject to a target error probability $\delta$ and an abstention budget $\alpha$, we propose Screen-and-Confirm (S&C) and analyze its expected stopping time. We further derive the minimum expected stopping time for any algorithm that satisfies these constraints. For Gaussian priors and rewards, as $(\delta,\alpha)\downarrow(0,0)$, we establish matching upper and lower bounds up to multiplicative constants, with rate $\kappa_\nu^2[1+\log((\alpha+\delta)/\delta)]/(\alpha+\delta)$, where $\kappa_\nu$ is the prior density of the top-two gap at zero, highlighting that nearly tied instances govern the sampling cost. When abstention is disallowed ($\alpha=0$), S&C yields the optimal $\Theta(1/\delta)$ dependence for fixed model parameters, removing the additional $\log(1/\delta)$ factor in the upper bound of Jang et al. (2024) under our Gaussian assumptions. We further characterize the exact multiplicative constant of the minimum expected stopping time for practical regimes including (i) fixed $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and (ii) $\alpha/\delta\to\infty$, which are also achieved by S&C.
core_methodology: Bayesian fixed-confidence best-arm identification with abstention, using a Screen-and-Confirm (S&C) approach to balance error probability and abstention budget
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any sequential decision-making scenario with Gaussian priors and rewards
alpha_potential: Potential application in trading system design where optimal stopping under uncertainty is crucial (e.g., early signal termination, dynamic strategy switching)
title_cn: 基于贝叶斯方法的固定置信度最优臂识别与弃权机制
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种在有弃权选项情况下的贝叶斯最优臂识别方法，通过'筛选后确认'机制平衡错误概率与采样成本。在量化交易领域，这种最优停止框架可应用于动态策略切换、早期信号评估等场景，特别适用于需要在高不确定性市场环境中做快速决策的交易系统。

title: Optimistic Policy Regularization: Elite-Statistic Reward Shaping
summary: On-policy agents discard trajectories after each update, including rare high-return episodes. We propose Optimistic Policy Regularization (OPR), which turns those episodes into a closed-form reward bonus: we estimate an elite action prior from top-quartile episodes and add a \reviewblue{bounded transform of the log-ratio} of the prior to the policy's action distribution. OPR needs no auxiliary network, value gate, off-policy correction, or adversarial loop. It is a one-line modification of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)'s reward; yet, on 49 Atari games at 10M steps, $5\times$ fewer agent decisions than the 200M-frame baselines, it reaches a 148.4\% median human-normalized score (HNS; 196.9\% interquartile mean): higher scores than published PPO on $36/49$ games ($p{=}0.0014$) and a higher aggregate median than self-imitation learning, which falls well below OPR when frames and backbone are matched. We pair the method with a theory of when it works. The underlying log-ratio has an exact forward-KL interpretation; its pre-advantage placement propagates the signal through Generalized Advantage Estimation; and, under an idealized local update, its first-order effect depends on a prior-advantage alignment whose sign indicates help or harm. Since alignment varies across tasks and runs, we also study an online gating extension. On a ten-game set, it outperforms the backbone by $+17.4$ median HNS on average across seeds. Controlled experiments test temporal propagation and the tradeoffs of state conditioning and gating, supporting OPR as a simple regularizer with an analysis of where to shape.
core_methodology: Optimistic Policy Regularization (OPR) is a reinforcement learning technique that enhances policy updates by incorporating a reward bonus based on elite action priors derived from top-performing trajectories. It modifies Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) rewards in a straightforward manner without requiring additional networks or complex corrections.
data_sources: Atari game environments (used as a testbed for RL algorithms)
alpha_potential: The method could be adapted to identify and exploit rare but high-reward market conditions, such as extreme momentum periods or arbitrage opportunities, by focusing policy updates on historically successful actions.
title_cn: 乐观策略正则化：精英统计奖励塑造
summary_cn: 乐观策略正则化（OPR）通过利用历史最优轨迹来增强策略更新，可应用于金融市场中识别和利用高回报机会。该方法简单高效，适合优化交易策略的高风险高回报决策场景。

title: Projecting Latent RL Actions: Towards Generalizable and Scalable Graph Combinatorial Optimization
summary: Graph combinatorial optimization (GCO) has attracted growing interest, as many NP-hard problems naturally admit graph formulations, yet their combinatorial explosion renders exact methods computationally intractable. Recent advances in Reinforcement Learning (RL) combined with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have significantly improved learning-based GCO solvers. However, existing approaches face limitations in both generalization across diverse graph instances and computational scalability as action spaces grow. To address both challenges, we introduce \textit{projection agents}, a GCO methodology built on the Wolpertinger framework and adapted to a shared GNN-based latent space for observations and actions. These agents are trained to solve GCO problems by predicting a desired latent action in a single forward pass, which is subsequently decoded into a valid discrete action in the graph using the latent space. Across diverse benchmarks, our approach achieves up to 6.41$\times$ faster inference and up to 75\% better generalization than existing solutions using a simple nearest-neighbor decoding, while opening the door to strong RL performance in super-linear decision spaces with multiple interdependent variables. Finally, we release \texttt{LaGCO-RL}, a Python library that automates latent action-space construction and supports existing RL-GCO solutions, promoting reproducibility and adaptation to new GCO benchmarks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a GCO methodology called projection agents, which combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to solve graph combinatorial optimization problems. The approach leverages a shared GNN-based latent space for observations and actions, enabling faster inference and better generalization across diverse graph instances through a nearest-neighbor decoding mechanism.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources, but it focuses on solving graph combinatorial optimization problems, which could be applied to financial data such as network-based market data, correlation graphs, or transaction networks.
alpha_potential: The methodology's potential lies in solving complex, NP-hard optimization problems efficiently, which could be valuable in portfolio optimization, trade execution, or other financial decision-making problems that can be formulated as graph combinatorial optimization tasks. However, direct financial applications are not yet demonstrated.
title_cn: 投射潜在强化学习动作：迈向可泛化和可扩展的图组合优化
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种结合强化学习和图神经网络的图组合优化方法，通过潜在动作空间实现快速推理和更好的泛化能力。在金融领域，该方法可能应用于投资组合优化、交易执行或其他可分解为图优化任务的决策问题，但具体应用仍需进一步研究。

title: DGA$_2$D: Directed Graph-Guided Automated Algorithm Design with Large Language Models
summary: The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened new avenues for Automated Heuristic Design (AHD) for solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). However, existing LLM-driven AHD methods are largely confined to rigid solver templates, relegating the search process to isolated module tuning. Transitioning to fully autonomous, system-level algorithm design is essential but fraught with low reliability of generated operators, extremely large search spaces, and ineffective credit assignment. To overcome these drawbacks, this paper proposes a Directed Graph-Guided Automated Algorithm Design framework, termed DGA$_2$D. It structures the open-ended program space as a directed graph, where each node represents a functional operator that can be instantiated using one of multiple candidate code implementations, while directed walks constitute complete algorithmic pipelines. A first-order path-dependent credit assignment mechanism is introduced to evaluate code variations strictly based on their topological context. Extensive experiments across 12 distinct COPs, ranging from complex scheduling to routing, demonstrate the consistent empirical advantages of DGA$_2$D. It reduces the average normalized gap by up to 10.96 percentage points compared to state-of-the-art LLM baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces DGA$_2$D, a framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate the design of algorithms for solving combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). It structures the program space as a directed graph, where nodes represent functional operators and walks constitute complete algorithmic pipelines. A credit assignment mechanism evaluates code variations based on their topological context.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on generic combinatorial optimization problems, which could hypothetically include financial problems like portfolio optimization or trade execution.
alpha_potential: If adapted to financial problems, the framework could potentially automate the design of trading strategies or portfolio optimization algorithms, leveraging LLMs to explore large search spaces efficiently.
title_cn: DGA$_2$D：基于有向图和大语言模型的自动化算法设计
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种利用大语言模型（LLMs）自动化设计组合优化问题算法的框架DGA$_2$D。通过将程序空间构建为有向图并进行路径依赖的信用分配，该框架在12种不同的组合优化问题中表现出显著优势。若应用于金融领域，可潜在地用于自动化交易策略设计或投资组合优化。

title: From Single-Actor Environments to Multi-Actor Event Worlds: Can LLMs Be Event World Models?
summary: World models help agents assess the consequences of their actions before acting. Many real systems, however, involve multiple actors who make their own decisions, can evolve even when the agent takes no action, and are only partially observed through event logs. We formalize these systems as event worlds and ask whether large language models can predict future observations from the log and the agent's proposed actions. We build complementary benchmarks from human Diplomacy games and real Polymarket trades. Our hierarchical framework compares prediction with and without other actors' actions, then tests multi-step rollouts, predictions for actions never taken, and usefulness to agents. Fine-tuning and more data improve prediction when all actors' recorded actions are given. With only the agent's action, models struggle when other actors strongly affect the outcome, and larger models and longer histories help little. This gap also limits multi-step prediction and agent decisions, with models overestimating plan success. Yet imagined experience and initialization from world models can still improve policy learning. Anticipating other actors' actions remains a central challenge for event world modeling.
core_methodology: Evaluating LLMs as event world models in multi-actor environments using hierarchical prediction frameworks
data_sources: Human Diplomacy games and real Polymarket trades
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability; explores prediction challenges in multi-agent systems which could inform some market microstructure models

title: Primal-Dual Representation Learning for Low-Rank Constrained MDPs
summary: Representation learning has substantially improved the efficiency of unconstrained continuous-state Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), but its extension to Constrained MDPs (CMDPs) is difficult because the transition representation must be learned while constraint violation is controlled. In this paper, we study representation learning for low-rank CMDPs with continuous state spaces, and propose REP-PD-TEG for the soft cumulative-violation setting. In the feature learning period, the algorithm interacts with the environment using a decaying-$\epsilon$-greedy mixture execution policy, and uses the collected samples to learn transition features by maximum likelihood. Based on the learned features, it constructs uncertainty bonuses and plans with an optimistic Lagrangian objective to obtain the return policy. We prove regret and soft-violation guarantees for the return policies, and quantify the influence of the decaying-$\epsilon$-greedy exploration. In particular, REP-PD-TEG achieves the optimal $\widetilde O(\sqrt K)$ return policy bound, and gives a $\widetilde O(K^{3/4})$ overall sample bound when exploratory actions are charged. For the stricter hard cumulative violation, where feasibility must be verified episode by episode, we propose REP-PD-H-TEG. It plans under a bonus-corrected lower-confidence utility certificate with the learned representation, and performs a stabilized dual search to obtain the return policy, yielding regret and hard-violation bounds. Together, these results give the first theoretically guaranteed representation-learning method for low-rank continuous-state CMDPs with both soft cumulative guarantees and certified hard-violation control.
core_methodology: Representation learning for constrained MDPs with low-rank structure, using primal-dual optimization and decaying-epsilon-greedy exploration
data_sources: Simulated environments (not financial data)
alpha_potential: Theoretical framework for constrained decision-making under uncertainty, but requires significant adaptation to financial markets

title: One Pretrained Decision Model Is Enough for Training-Free Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection
summary: Graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to identify irregular entities in graph-structured data, yet heterogeneous anomaly patterns and distributional differences across graphs challenge generalizable detection. Existing training-free approaches avoid task-specific optimization but primarily rely on predefined numerical scoring rules, leaving the semantic interpretation of heterogeneous anomaly evidence largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose Jev-GAD, a training-free generalist graph anomaly detection framework that bridges heterogeneous numerical evidence and pretrained decision mechanisms. To address heterogeneous anomaly patterns, we construct complementary structural, attribute, and neighborhood evidence and transform heterogeneous statistics into graph-relative anomaly percentiles. To move beyond predefined numerical scoring rules, we leverage a single frozen pretrained language model for evidence-conditioned anomaly assessment. To bridge the semantic gap between numerical evidence and pretrained models, we design a semantic Graph-to-State (G2S) transformation that organizes graph context and semantically labeled node evidence into structured decision states for non-generative option-logit readout. The resulting decision scores are integrated with four complementary statistical scores through equal-weight rank-based fusion, without GAD-specific gradient-based optimization. Extensive experiments on seven graph anomaly detection benchmarks spanning citation, social, and co-review networks demonstrate the effectiveness of Jev-GAD, achieving average AUROC and AUPRC scores of 89.18\% and 52.40\%, respectively. Further analyses validate the contributions of pretrained decision readout and semantic evidence grounding.
core_methodology: Training-free generalist graph anomaly detection framework utilizing pretrained language models for evidence-conditioned anomaly assessment without task-specific optimization
data_sources: Graph-structured data (citation, social, and co-review networks, but not financial networks specifically)
alpha_potential: Potential for detecting anomalous patterns in graph-structured financial data (e.g., payment networks, social sentiment graphs), but not directly demonstrated on financial datasets

title: Semi-Linear Gaussian Bayesian Networks: Enhancing Flexibility in Node Dependencies via penalized B-Splines
summary: Bayesian networks for continuous variables often rely on restrictive assumptions: linear Gaussian models lack flexibility to capture nonlinear dependencies, while non-parametric approaches provide greater flexibility at a high computational cost. This creates a gap for modeling scenarios where variables are approximately Gaussian but exhibit nonlinear relationships. We introduce Semi-Linear Gaussian Bayesian Networks (SLGBN), a novel class of continuous Bayesian networks designed to bridge this gap, preserving Gaussian conditional distributions while introducing nonlinear conditional mean functions. The proposed framework provides a unified probabilistic framework combining linear Gaussian and nonlinear Gaussian conditional models within the same Bayesian network Nonlinear conditional mean functions are estimated using generalized additive models (GAMs) with penalized B-splines. We present parameter estimation procedures for both types of nodes, as well as a greedy hill-climbing algorithm for learning the network structure under the SLGBN framework. To assess its performance, we compare SLGBN with other continuous Bayesian network models, including semiparametric Bayesian networks (SPBN) and Linear Gaussian Bayesian networks (LGBN). Experimental results evaluate both goodness of fit and the ability to recover the underlying network structure. The results show that, in the presence of nonlinear Gaussian relationships, SLGBN achieves better fit and improved structure recovery compared to alternative models, particularly when combined with the Extended Bayesian Information Criterion (EBIC*) score. Furthermore, by retaining Gaussian conditional distributions, SLGBN offers computational advantages over fully semiparametric approaches.
core_methodology: Semi-Linear Gaussian Bayesian Networks (SLGBN) combining linear and nonlinear Gaussian conditional models with penalized B-splines
data_sources: Not specified (experimental data likely synthetic or non-financial)
alpha_potential: Potential for modeling nonlinear relationships in financial data, but lacks direct trading strategy applications

title: Parameter Learning in Active Inference via Variational Message Passing
summary: Active inference casts perception, learning and planning as variational inference, where the Expected Free Energy (EFE) defines the planning objective. Recent work showed that EFE minimization can be written as Variational Free Energy (VFE) minimization on a generative model augmented with epistemic priors, and that the resulting entropy-corrected objective is minimized by sum-product message passing (SP-MP) on modified factor functions. These formulations treat model uncertainty as inference over a finite set of known models. We extend them to planning during learning, where beliefs over the observation and transition parameters $\theta_A$, $\theta_B$ are Dirichlet priors. Closed-form Dirichlet updates are usually obtained by a structured mean-field factorization between parameters and states, but under exactly that factorization the information-gain corrections vanish. We resolve this by giving every factor its own parameter prior, frozen during a rollout. Conjugacy then makes each factor belief a product of a marginal over the categorical variables and a one-step Bayes posterior of the parameters. This reintroduces the datum-dependent parameter posteriors that mean-field factorization destroys. We show that evaluating the epistemic priors under the resulting Bethe joint recovers the information gains. Stationarity of this single closed-form objective yields SP-MP whose factor functions are augmented by the information-gain weight. Experiments on two grid POMDPs, in which only a planner that learns the model finds the safe route, show that the method plans to efficiently learn $\theta_A$ and $\theta_B$. It reaches the goal on every episode, whereas SP-MP planners with the same inference update plateau or take the risky route.
core_methodology: Active inference and variational message passing for parameter learning in probabilistic models
data_sources: Simulated environments/grid POMDPs (not market data)
alpha_potential: Theoretical framework for learning under uncertainty, but no direct financial implementation demonstrated

title: Random Initialization as a Baseline for Time Series Foundation Models
summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) use self-supervised pretraining to learn reusable representations for downstream tasks such as multivariate time series classification (MTSC). We examine how much pretrained weights contribute beyond the architecture itself by comparing seven publicly released instances from four TSFM families with architecture-matched randomly initialized counterparts on the UEA MTSC archive. For each instance, five random initializations are evaluated using four classifiers on frozen representations: ridge classification, logistic regression, RBF SVM, and random forest. After model-specific exclusions due to computational constraints, the study comprises 183 paired dataset-level comparisons. Pretraining improves mean accuracy for all seven instances, but the gains are modest, ranging from 1.43 to 5.19 percentage points, with an overall average improvement of 2.58 points. Three of seven per-instance Wilcoxon signed-rank tests have raw $p$-values below 0.05, but only NuTime remains significant after Holm correction. A secondary pooled test across all 183 pairs gives $p < 0.001$, while the corrected per-instance tests remain the primary evidence. We also compare with ROCKET, Hydra, and Quant, which remain competitive without requiring large-scale pretraining. These findings suggest that MTSC evaluations should distinguish the effect of pretrained weights from that of the underlying architecture and should include both architecture-matched random initialization and strong non-pretrained baselines.
core_methodology: Comparison of pretrained time series foundation models with architecture-matched randomly initialized counterparts on multivariate time series classification tasks
data_sources: UEA MTSC archive
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability, but suggests that architectural choices may be more important than pretraining for time series analysis, which could inform feature engineering in financial time series

title: Is High Local Accuracy Enough? Geometric Consensus with Support-Adaptive Statistical Personalization for Federated Learning
summary: Real-world deployment of personalized federated learning (PFL) requires adapting to heterogeneous clients while preserving recognition performance beyond local distributions. However, high local accuracy can conceal failures on locally rare or absent classes. Effective personalization should therefore strengthen global recognition while raising the personalization floor. We propose an evaluation protocol that complements local accuracy with global, rare-class, and unseen-class evaluations to reveal generalization obscured by local scores, and assesses personalization floors among the worst-performing clients to expose weaknesses hidden by aggregate performance. To meet these deployment challenges, we propose FedGRC, a unified PFL framework integrating generalization and personalization through (i) Consensus-Guided Representation Learning (CGRL), which learns discriminative representations through shared directional and magnitude guidance; (ii) Multilayer Metric Synthesis (MMS), which constructs a shared covariance metric from these multilayer representations for statistical classification; and (iii) Support-Adaptive Shrinkage Personalization (SASP), which adapts class means within this metric by shrinking local estimates toward shared means according to local sample support, enabling adaptation while retaining shared knowledge. Extensive experiments, including benchmarking against 21 methods across 5 heterogeneity settings on 3 datasets and comprehensive ablation studies, validate the effectiveness of FedGRC. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, FedGRC surpasses state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines in global recognition and personalization floors by at least 2.17% and 2.13%, respectively. On the real-world heterogeneous FedRS dataset, it outperforms the respective best baselines by 2.15%, 3.30%, and 4.61% in local adaptation, global recognition, and the personalization floor.
core_methodology: Federated Learning with Consensus-Guided Representation Learning, Multilayer Metric Synthesis, and Support-Adaptive Shrinkage Personalization
data_sources: Standard image datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100) and a real-world heterogeneous dataset (FedRS)
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability to trading; methodology focuses on improving model generalization and personalization in non-financial contexts

title: The Bayesian Learning Rule Beyond KL Geometry
summary: The Bayesian learning rule (BLR) exploits the relation between Bayesian updating and the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD) to derive efficient additive updates for exponential family variational posteriors. The KL geometry is powerful but restrictive: combined with posterior families with parameter-dependent support it can lead to undefined objectives. We ask which non-KL geometries preserve the additive BLR computation. Previous works that use $f$-divergences suggest that this is only possible with the KLD. Here, we show that this is not true. We show that additive information-geometric optimization algorithms can be derived for the class of mixed-space Bregman or Fenchel-Young discrepancies. These discrepancies induce generalized maximum-entropy families, dual coordinates, and generalized-BLR canonical gradient updates, recovering the classical BLR. The generalized BLR leads to new algorithms that \textit{cannot} be derived from the KL-based BLR. For the Tsallis negentropy with quadratic statistics, the generalized BLR yields bounded-support and heavy-tailed $q$-Gaussian posteriors and an easy Newton-like implementation. Experiments up to CIFAR-100 illustrate controllable support and tail behavior and competitive performance.
core_methodology: Generalized Bayesian learning rule using mixed-space Bregman/Fenchel-Young discrepancies for non-KL variational inference
data_sources: Not financial data (tested on CIFAR-100 computer vision dataset)
alpha_potential: Potential theoretical framework for heavy-tailed posterior modeling in market microstructure analysis

title: Lifetime-valid decisions by continually evolving AI analysts
summary: AI agents increasingly act as analysts whose decision can often be cast as hypothesis tests. Classical tests control the Type I error rate, the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis, for fixed procedures. However, AI analysts introduce internal randomness and can evolve continuously over time. As AI analysts evolve, the risk of approving versions with Type I error rates above the target can accumulate, and adaptive use of evaluation feedback can lead to overfitting. We introduce continual validation, which evaluates each proposed AI analyst version before deployment using simulated data under the null hypothesis, with scenarios that can be randomized and expanded over time. We prove that, regardless of how updates are chosen or how many are proposed, the lifetime probability of ever deploying a version whose Type I error rate exceeds the allowed level remains bounded. This guarantees that every subsequent decision controls the Type I error rate at the target level across these scenarios. At the same time, updates with sufficiently low Type I error rates pass validation with high probability, allowing the analyst to continuously improve its performance without sacrificing rigor. In two examples involving evolving AI analysts for bioequivalence studies and product A/B tests, Type I error rates reached 0.098 and 0.183 without continual validation, compared with at most 0.045 and 0.044 with it, while retaining 82% and 96% of the power from optimally selected valid updates.
core_methodology: Continual validation process for evolving AI analysts using simulated data under null hypothesis to control Type I error rates over time
data_sources: Simulated data under null hypothesis (not financial market data)
alpha_potential: Potential to improve statistical validity of algorithmic decisions in trading systems, but no direct trading signal generation demonstrated

title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
summary: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. Based on this information, we must decide whether to accept the AI decision automatically or consult an expert, such as a human auditor, who reviews the proposal and either accepts or corrects it. We formulate this task as an online constrained optimization problem in which the goal is to minimize the frequency of expert auditing while guaranteeing that the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited stays below a user-defined threshold. We derive a family of algorithms with provable error-control guarantees with no assumptions, including a method that is optimally efficient: it asymptotically attains the best achievable auditing rate for both adversarial and i.i.d. data streams. Experiments on screening harmful requests to large language models, qualitative text annotation, and data labeling show that our methods achieve valid error control in practice while substantially reducing the need for human auditing compared to baselines.
core_methodology: Online constrained optimization for auditing AI decisions with provable error-control guarantees
data_sources: Generic AI system outputs (confidence scores and decisions), not financial-specific
alpha_potential: Potential to reduce manual verification costs in AI-assisted trading systems, but no direct trading signal generation

title: Risk-Aware Alignment Must Incorporate Reward Uncertainty
summary: We consider the problem of policy optimization with noisy rewards, where the policy is constrained to be in the neighborhood of a reference policy.We study the risk of the policy optimization process, defined to be the chance of obtaining a policy worse off than the reference policy. In an idealized multivariate Gaussian model for the noisy reward function, we show that the regularizer achieving optimal risk in a suitably local neighborhood of the reference policy is the quadratic norm weighted by the reward covariance matrix. This result is used to develop a new policy optimization algorithm based on regularization via reward variance estimates. Experiments across synthetic bandit models, large language models and reward models show that this algorithm yields more robust alignment outcomes than existing approaches.
core_methodology: Policy optimization with noisy rewards using quadratic norm regularization weighted by reward covariance matrix
data_sources: Synthetic bandit models, large language models, and reward models
alpha_potential: Potential for more robust policy optimization under reward uncertainty, but financial market applications require significant adaptation

title: Fragility-aware Classification for Risk Characterization and Robust Learning
summary: Classification models play a central role in data-driven decision-making applications such as medical diagnosis, recommendation systems, and risk assessment. Traditional performance metrics, such as accuracy and AUC, quantify classification errors and pairwise ranking performance but do not account for the magnitude of errors, i.e., the risk of confident misjudgments. This limitation is particularly consequential in safety-critical and cost-sensitive settings, where overconfident errors can lead to severe outcomes. To address this issue, we propose the Fragility Index (FI), a novel performance metric that evaluates classifiers from a risk-averse perspective by capturing the tail risk of confident misjudgments. We formulate FI within a robust satisficing (RS) framework to quantify classifier sensitivity under distributional uncertainty. Building on this, we develop a tractable surrogate-based training framework and establish provable bounds connecting training fragility to ranking-error FI. We further derive tractable reformulations for a broad class of loss functions, including cross-entropy, hinge-type, and Lipschitz losses, and identify specific conditions under which these reformulations are exact. We also introduce an FI-induced regularizer for deep neural networks. Empirical results on real-world medical diagnosis tasks demonstrate that FI complements existing metrics by revealing error tail risk not reflected in accuracy or AUC. FI-based models achieve competitive predictive performance while generally attaining lower FI. In the simulated human--AI diagnostic workflow, they also achieve lower average operational costs than empirical risk minimization.
core_methodology: Introduction of Fragility Index (FI) for risk-averse classifier evaluation within robust satisficing framework
data_sources: Medical diagnosis datasets (non-financial)
alpha_potential: Low direct applicability in trading, but FI concept could potentially be adapted for tail risk assessment in strategy backtesting

title: Analysis of On-policy Policy Gradient Methods under the Distribution Mismatch
summary: Policy gradient methods are among the most successful approaches for solving challenging reinforcement learning problems. Despite their empirical success, many state-of-the-art policy gradient algorithms for discounted problems estimate update directions using a sampling distribution that differs from the discounted state distribution required by the policy gradient theorem. In this work, we analyze the impact of this distribution mismatch on policy gradient methods. Specifically, {for tabular direct and softmax parameterizations, we establish global convergence of objective values under biased updates}. {For tabular softmax policies, we further derive the exact leading-order coefficients of the asymptotic objective errors under biased and normalized exact updates. Their ratio provides an explicit criterion for determining when distribution mismatch accelerates or slows asymptotic convergence.} We then extend the analysis to more general policy parameterizations by deriving explicit bounds on both the state distribution mismatch and the induced normalized policy-gradient mismatch in episodic and continuing MDPs. These mismatches vanish at least linearly as the discount factor approaches one. Under an additional smoothness assumption, we further show that the limit inferior of the squared norm of the normalized exact policy-gradient direction along the biased iterates is bounded by $O((1-\gamma)^2)$ in both settings. Our results provide theoretical insights into the robustness of policy gradient methods to distribution mismatch and shed light on the gap between their theoretical formulations and practical implementations.
core_methodology: Analysis of policy gradient methods in reinforcement learning, focusing on distribution mismatch effects
data_sources: Theoretical analysis based on episodic and continuing Markov Decision Processes (MDPs)
alpha_potential: Limited direct application to trading; potential insights for RL-based trading algorithms under distribution shifts

title: Graph Memory Transformer (GMT)
summary: We investigate whether an explicit learned memory graph can replace the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) sublayer in a decoder-only transformer while preserving the surrounding autoregressive architecture. In the proposed graph Memory Transformer (GMT), a memory cell routes token representations over a learned bank of centroids connected by a learned directed transition matrix, while causal self-attention remains unchanged. In the base v7 instantiation, each of 16 transformer blocks contains 128 centroids and a 128 x 128 edge matrix. Each cell uses gravitational source routing and token-conditioned target selection to return a gated displacement from the estimated source memory state toward the target memory state, rather than a retrieved value. The resulting decoder-only language model has 82.2M trainable parameters and no dense FFN sublayers; the evaluated dense GPT-style baseline has 103.0M. It trains stably and exposes centroid usage, transition structure, and source-to-target movement for direct inspection in the forward computation. It trails the larger baseline in validation loss and perplexity (3.5995/36.58 vs. 3.2903/26.85), while showing close zero-shot benchmark behavior under the evaluated setting. These results support the viability and structural interpretability of replacing dense within-token transformation with graph-mediated memory navigation, without claiming state-of-the-art performance. Broader scaling, optimized kernels, and more extensive benchmark evaluation remain for future work.
core_methodology: Replaces FFN sublayers in transformers with graph-based memory navigation using learned centroids and transition matrices
data_sources: Not explicitly financial data, tested as language model architecture
alpha_potential: Potential for interpretable sequence modeling but unproven for financial time series

title: WhatIf-Bench: Benchmarking Intervention-Aware Time Series Forecasting
summary: Recent time series foundation models (TSFMs) can consume covariates in-context, extending zero-shot forecasting to problems driven by external factors. This enables scenario analysis: forecasting how a target responds to events that set covariates to chosen future values. Whether they can do this reliably is an open question. We introduce WhatIf-Bench, a benchmark measuring how well forecasters use covariates to forecast a target's response to future events. WhatIf-Bench is semi-synthetic: time series come from mechanistic simulators of data centers, power grids, road traffic, and water networks, with controlled covariate-target relationships grounded in each system. Each task presents a history of events intervening on covariates, then asks to forecast a future event that either replays seen values (Replay) or sets them to unseen ones (Novel). Varying the number of covariates, historical events, and event length yields 37,665 tasks. Evaluating TSFMs, frontier LLMs, and simple regression baselines, we find the LLMs reach the highest skill (improvement over a naive baseline), ahead of the best TSFMs. Every model forecasts well on Replay futures (48 to 85% skill) but drops to -7 to 50% on Novel futures, with the regression baselines falling the most. Skill on Novel futures also falls as events set more covariates jointly. More historical events raise skill on Novel futures across the board, but large differences remain. WhatIf-Bench reveals generalization to Novel futures as the core challenge, and offers a testbed toward arbitrary scenario analysis.
core_methodology: Benchmarking time series forecasting models on their ability to handle interventions on covariates for scenario analysis
data_sources: Semi-synthetic data from mechanistic simulators (data centers, power grids, road traffic, water networks)
alpha_potential: Limited direct trading application; potentially useful for understanding exogenous factor impacts in specific controlled environments

title: baseVultra: Compact Nonlinear Recurrence with Reallocated Capacity
summary: Nonlinear recurrent networks remain useful for streaming sequence modeling, yet gated cell design is still dominated by LSTM and GRU. We study whether recurrent computation can be reallocated away from gate transforms and toward candidate generation. We propose baseVultra, a compact recurrent cell that concentrates the dense recurrent budget on a single H x H candidate-generation matrix, while replacing recurrent gate matrices with O(H) diagonal interactions. The candidate update combines this dense branch with two low-rank auxiliary branches, an EMA cache, and learnable output blending; the gates additionally receive lightweight second-order access to h_{t-2} through diagonal terms. On TinyShakespeare character-level language modeling, baseVultra achieves a validation loss of 1.594 in the compact one-layer 200K setting, compared with 1.604 for a parameter-matched LSTM and 1.616 for a parameter-matched GRU, while its dense recurrent matrix-vector computation is about 54% of GRU under matched hidden size for this configuration. On text8, a roughly 45x larger benchmark, baseVultra is competitive with full-gate cells (1.854 bpc vs. 1.849 for GRU and 1.837 for LSTM). On formal-language probes, the largest gains appear under constrained hidden-state capacity (0.991 vs. 0.761 GRU and 0.691 LSTM OOD2 accuracy on Counter at H=16) and vanish as hidden size grows. These results characterize where and when candidate-focused recurrent capacity allocation helps: the benefit is concentrated in compact regimes, while full-gate cells remain competitive at scale.
core_methodology: Proposes a compact recurrent cell (baseVultra) that reallocates computation from gate transforms to candidate generation, using a single dense matrix for candidates and diagonal interactions for gates
data_sources: Benchmark datasets for language modeling (TinyShakespeare, text8) and formal-language probes
alpha_potential: Limited direct trading applicability; potential theoretical value for compact time-series models but not demonstrated on financial data

title: Is spectral predictability enough? Testing {\Omega}-matching for synthetic pretraining under distribution shift
summary: Synthetic pretraining under distribution shift requires deciding what synthetic data to use. A natural criterion is to match the spectral predictability $\Omega$ of the source to the target, but is $\Omega$ sufficient? We test this hypothesis, which we call predictability-aware pretraining, across three architectures (LSTM, PatchTST, TCN) and three seeds. Under ideal synthetic-to-synthetic conditions, $\Omega$-matched pretraining can outperform even an oracle baseline (+46.8% MSE reduction, LSTM), though the benefit is already architecture-dependent. On the real-world ETTm1 benchmark, however, this relationship does not hold: sine-plus-noise pretraining at matched $\Omega$ yields only a marginal mean improvement +2.3% averaged over all three architectures, up to +65.5% on individual channels), whereas $\Omega$ matched chaotic ODE trajectories systematically degrade performance -13.2%). The two sources agree on the direction of transfer for only 53% of configurations across all three architectures (Pearson r=-0.02), indicating that $\Omega$ carries little information about which source will transfer beneficially. We further observe an architecture-dependent asymmetry in the response to the direction of the $\Omega$ gap. We conclude that $\Omega$ matching can help in controlled settings but is not sufficient to predict transfer across sources, and we discuss additional signal properties that a source-selection criterion may need to consider.
core_methodology: Testing spectral predictability (Omega-matching) for synthetic pretraining under distribution shift
data_sources: ETTm1 benchmark and synthetic data (sine-plus-noise, chaotic ODE trajectories)
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability; explores theoretical aspects of data selection for pretraining without clear financial market implications

title: Federated Differentially Private Optimization via Low-Rank Preconditioning
summary: We consider differentially private (DP) optimization in the federated setting, where a DP estimate of the feature covariance matrix serves as a Hessian approximation for generalized linear models. Existing central DP methods for covariance estimation have communication cost that grows quadratically in the data dimension, while existing baselines with linear communication cost are only locally private and degrade as the number of clients increases. As a remedy, we propose a federated DP-PCA framework that achieves linear communication cost while providing central DP guarantees under secure aggregation. It consists of a DP rank selection step, a DP power method, and a noisy release of the covariance projected onto the selected low-dimensional subspace. We give error bounds for this covariance estimate and for the resulting low-communication preconditioned DP gradient descent. Empirically, our proposed DP optimization method matches a centralized baseline with quadratic communication cost at a fraction of the communication.
core_methodology: Federated differential privacy (DP) optimization with low-rank preconditioning
data_sources: Federated data sources (cross-client/silo data sharing scenarios)
alpha_potential: Potentially useful for secure cross-institutional model training where data cannot be pooled

title: Group Contrastive Policy Optimization: Learning Beyond the Self-Exploration Limit with Golden Answers
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning abilities of large language models, yet group-based methods lose their learning signal when every sampled response receives zero reward. We propose Group Contrastive Policy Optimization (GCPO), a hybrid objective that preserves standard on-policy optimization for informative rollout groups and activates a proximal contrastive objective only when exploration completely fails.
